title: Factors associated with vaccination against Seasonal Influenza and SARS-CoV-2 in the UK among FluSurvey participants, 2023-2025.
abstract: Seasonal Influenza and COVID-19 vaccination programmes are critical for reducing morbidity and mortality in older adults, yet uptake remains uneven across populations. We aimed to profile vaccination attitudes and examine predictors of COVID-19/influenza vaccination uptake among a UK participatory surveillance system - FluSurvey. We analysed FluSurvey data from participants aged [≥]65 years who were eligible for both vaccines in the 2023-2024 and 2024-2025 Autumn - Winter seasonal campaigns. Descriptive analyses examined self-reported attitudes to influenza vaccination. Logistic regression examined factors (age, sex, socioeconomic status, education, employment, transport, smoking and chronic conditions) associated with influenza and COVID-19 vaccination uptake in each season, adjusting for confounders. Belonging to a risk group and reducing risk of influenza were frequently reported motivations for influenza vaccination, while building natural immunity and concerns around safety and adverse effects were frequently reported barriers. Individuals vaccinated against COVID-19 were more likely to receive an influenza vaccination (aOR2023-2024=13.90 [9.28-21.17]; aOR2024-2025=8.54 [5.82-12.60]), and vice-versa (aOR2023-2024=13.91 [9.30-21.19]; aOR2024-2025=8.52 [5.81-12.58]). Lower educational attainment was associated with lower odds of COVID-19 vaccination (aOR2023-2024=0.59 [0.45-0.78], aOR2024-2025: 0.56 [0.39-0.79]). Other results were weaker or demonstrated variation by season. Our findings highlight recent attitudes and barriers to influenza and COVID-19 vaccination among the FluSurvey cohort, which may inform approaches to improve vaccination coverage in the population.

The central question is to profile vaccination attitudes and identify predictors of vaccine uptake for both pathogens.
analysis.evidence_base_and_review_method: The review analyzed FluSurvey data from participants aged ≥65 years who were eligible for both vaccines. Descriptive analyses were conducted to explore self-reported attitudes toward influenza vaccination.

Further research is needed to explore the seasonal variations in vaccine uptake and to address the evidence gaps in understanding the factors influencing vaccination behavior.

analysis.summary_en: This review examines factors associated with vaccination against Seasonal Influenza and SARS-CoV-2 in the UK among FluSurvey participants aged ≥65 years during the 2023-2024 and 2024-2025 Autumn-Winter campaigns. It profiles vaccination attitudes and identifies predictors of vaccine uptake, including risk group membership and educational attainment. The review finds that individuals vaccinated against one pathogen are more likely to receive the other, but other factors show weaker or inconsistent associations. It highlights the need for targeted strategies to improve vaccination coverage and suggests further research to address seasonal variations and evidence gaps in understanding vaccine behavior.

elements_zh.scope_and_question: 该综述重点关注 季节性流感 病毒,特别研究了 2023-2024 年和 2024-2025 年秋冬季运动期间英国流感调查参与者中与 季节性流感 和 SARS-CoV-2 相关的 疫苗接种 相关因素。核心问题是分析 疫苗接种 态度并确定两种病原体 疫苗 摄取的预测因子。
elements_zh.evidence_base_and_review_method: 该综述分析了年龄≥65岁且符合 疫苗 资格的参与者的流感调查数据。使用逻辑回归来检查与流感和 COVID-19 疫苗接种 摄取相关的因素(年龄、性别、社会经济地位、教育、就业、交通、吸烟和慢性病),并调整混杂因素。进行描述性分析以探讨自我报告的对流感 疫苗接种 的态度。
elements_zh.consensus_and_key_conclusions: 经常报道的流感 疫苗接种 的动机是属于风险群体和降低流感风险。对安全性和不良反应的担忧是常见的障碍。接种了 COVID-19 疫苗的个体更有可能感染流感 疫苗接种,反之亦然,表明 疫苗 摄取这两种病原体之间存在潜在关联。
elements_zh.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: 较低的教育程度与较低的 COVID-19 疫苗接种 几率相关。其他结果较弱或随季节变化而变化,表明研究结果的一致性有限。该综述没有提供有关目标与相关实体之间的生物学或分类学关系的详细信息,也没有解决理解这些关系方面的具体差距。
elements_zh.research_and_practice_implications: 研究结果强调了流感调查 队列研究 中最近对流感和 COVID-19 疫苗接种 的态度和障碍,这可能为提高 疫苗接种 在人群中覆盖率的策略提供参考。需要进一步的研究来探索 疫苗 吸收的季节性变化,并解决在理解影响 疫苗接种 行为的因素方面的证据差距。

analysis_zh.scope_and_question: 该综述重点关注 季节性流感 病毒,特别研究了 2023-2024 年和 2024-2025 年秋冬季运动期间英国流感调查参与者中与 季节性流感 和 SARS-CoV-2 相关的 疫苗接种 相关因素。核心问题是分析 疫苗接种 态度并确定两种病原体 疫苗 摄取的预测因子。

title: N-linked glycosylation sites with low occupancy support sustained circulation of the A(H3N2) influenza A virus in the human population.
abstract: ABSTRACT Glycosylation of the influenza A virus hemagglutinin is crucial for viral fitness and immune evasion. The hemagglutinin of contemporary human A(H3N2) influenza A viruses is extensively glycosylated with up to 13 putative glycosylation sites. Glycan types and occupancy of these sites are not uniform: while most are nearly completely occupied by glycans, some, such as those at amino acid residues 45 and 144, are only partially occupied and are evolutionarily unstable. While the effects of highly occupied glycosylated sites of hemagglutinin on A(H3N2) influenza A virus biology are well studied, there is limited information on the functional impact of the low-occupancy glycosylation sites on the viral hemagglutinin. Here, by using reverse-genetics A(H3N2) influenza A viruses lacking glycans at either residue 45 or 144, or both in hemagglutinin, we demonstrate that, despite reduced receptor binding, thermal stability, and fusion, the presence of a low level of glycosylation at these positions does not impact virus growth in Madin-Darby canine kidney epithelial cell culture. In contrast, these low-occupancy sites do affect immune responses in mice, by reducing titers of antibodies that correlate with virus neutralization and protection against influenza disease. We suggest that the temporary introduction of sites with low glycosylation allows influenza viruses to reduce the immune pressure on antigenic and receptor binding sites of hemagglutinin without significantly compromising viral virulence. This mechanism may help support the sustained circulation of A(H3N2) influenza A virus in human populations. IMPORTANCE Many of the glycosylation sites on the hemagglutinin of influenza A viruses are near antigenic sites, such that the glycans block antibody recognition and help evade population immunity. However, glycans may also reduce viral replication and virulence. Glycosylation sites at amino acid residues 45 and 144 of the hemagglutinin of contemporary A(H3N2) influenza A viruses are minimally occupied, with fewer than 10% of the sites containing glycans. This is still sufficient to partially evade antibody-based population immunity, while minimizing the impact on replication and virulence. Over time, A(H3N2) viruses have used both these sites only during limited periods, suggesting that even a low level of glycan occupancy may confer some negative selection pressure that is compensated by evasion of human population immunity. Data from this study provide a better understanding of the mechanisms that allow viruses to evade antibody-based immunity and maintain circulation in the human population. However, glycans may also reduce viral replication and virulence.

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to investigate the functional impact of low-occupancy glycosylation sites on the hemagglutinin of A(H3N2) influenza A viruses and their role in immune evasion and viral persistence.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study involved reverse-genetics to generate A(H3N2) influenza A viruses lacking glycans at specific hemagglutinin residues, and tested these viruses in Madin-Darby canine kidney epithelial cell culture and in mice.
analysis.methods: The researchers used reverse-genetics to create A(H3N2) influenza A viruses with modified glycosylation sites at residues 45 and 144, and assessed their effects on viral growth in cell culture and immune responses in mice.
analysis.main_results: The presence of low glycosylation at residues 45 and 144 did not affect virus growth in cell culture, but it reduced antibody titers in mice that correlate with virus neutralization and protection against influenza disease.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors suggest that low-occupancy glycosylation sites may help influenza viruses reduce immune pressure on key antigenic sites without significantly compromising virulence, offering a novel insight into viral immune evasion strategies.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: These findings may inform strategies for vaccine design and surveillance by highlighting the role of low-occupancy glycosylation sites in maintaining viral circulation and immune evasion in human populations.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited to in vitro and in vivo models, and the evidence is moderate as it does not include long-term population-level data or clinical outcomes.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigates the functional impact of low-occupancy glycosylation sites on the hemagglutinin of A(H3N2) influenza A viruses. It demonstrates that despite reduced receptor binding and thermal stability, these sites do not hinder viral growth in cell culture. However, they do affect immune responses in mice by reducing antibody titers associated with neutralization and protection. The authors propose that these sites may help the virus evade immune pressure while maintaining virulence, supporting its sustained circulation in human populations. The study uses reverse-genetics and animal models, which provide moderate evidence but lack direct clinical data. These findings could inform vaccine development and surveillance strategies for seasonal influenza viruses.

analysis_en.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to investigate the functional impact of low-occupancy glycosylation sites on the hemagglutinin of A(H3N2) influenza A viruses and their role in immune evasion and viral persistence.
analysis_en.study_design_and_population: The study involved reverse-genetics to generate A(H3N2) influenza A viruses lacking glycans at specific hemagglutinin residues, and tested these viruses in Madin-Darby canine kidney epithelial cell culture and in mice.
analysis_en.methods: The researchers used reverse-genetics to create A(H3N2) influenza A viruses with modified glycosylation sites at residues 45 and 144, and assessed their effects on viral growth in cell culture and immune responses in mice.
analysis_en.main_results: The presence of low glycosylation at residues 45 and 144 did not affect virus growth in cell culture, but it reduced antibody titers in mice that correlate with virus neutralization and protection against influenza disease.
analysis_en.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors suggest that low-occupancy glycosylation sites may help influenza viruses reduce immune pressure on key antigenic sites without significantly compromising virulence, offering a novel insight into viral immune evasion strategies.
analysis_en.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: These findings may inform strategies for vaccine design and surveillance by highlighting the role of low-occupancy glycosylation sites in maintaining viral circulation and immune evasion in human populations.
analysis_en.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited to in vitro and in vivo models, and the evidence is moderate as it does not include long-term population-level data or clinical outcomes.

title_zh: 低占用率的 N 连接糖基化位点支持 甲型H3N2流感病毒 甲型流感病毒在人群中持续循环。
source_body_en: ABSTRACT Glycosylation of the influenza A virus hemagglutinin is crucial for viral fitness and immune evasion. The hemagglutinin of contemporary human A(H3N2) influenza A viruses is extensively glycosylated with up to 13 putative glycosylation sites. Glycan types and occupancy of these sites are not uniform: while most are nearly completely occupied by glycans, some, such as those at amino acid residues 45 and 144, are only partially occupied and are evolutionarily unstable. While the effects of highly occupied glycosylated sites of hemagglutinin on A(H3N2) influenza A virus biology are well studied, there is limited information on the functional impact of the low-occupancy glycosylation sites on the viral hemagglutinin. Here, by using reverse-genetics A(H3N2) influenza A viruses lacking glycans at either residue 45 or 144, or both in hemagglutinin, we demonstrate that, despite reduced receptor binding, thermal stability, and fusion, the presence of a low level of glycosylation at these positions does not impact virus growth in Madin-Darby canine kidney epithelial cell culture. In contrast, these low-occupancy sites do affect immune responses in mice, by reducing titers of antibodies that correlate with virus neutralization and protection against influenza disease. We suggest that the temporary introduction of sites with low glycosylation allows influenza viruses to reduce the immune pressure on antigenic and receptor binding sites of hemagglutinin without significantly compromising viral virulence. This mechanism may help support the sustained circulation of A(H3N2) influenza A virus in human populations. IMPORTANCE Many of the glycosylation sites on the hemagglutinin of influenza A viruses are near antigenic sites, such that the glycans block antibody recognition and help evade population immunity. However, glycans may also reduce viral replication and virulence. Glycosylation sites at amino acid residues 45 and 144 of the hemagglutinin of contemporary A(H3N2) influenza A viruses are minimally occupied, with fewer than 10% of the sites containing glycans. This is still sufficient to partially evade antibody-based population immunity, while minimizing the impact on replication and virulence. Over time, A(H3N2) viruses have used both these sites only during limited periods, suggesting that even a low level of glycan occupancy may confer some negative selection pressure that is compensated by evasion of human population immunity. Data from this study provide a better understanding of the mechanisms that allow viruses to evade antibody-based immunity and maintain circulation in the human population. However, glycans may also reduce viral replication and virulence.

title: Deciphering influenza B virus-derived peptides and their presentation by HLA class I molecules.
abstract: Despite influenza vaccines being widely available, influenza still causes significant morbidity and mortality annually. Vaccines typically induce humoral-mediated protection against rapidly mutating surface glycoproteins, necessitating that they be updated and administered each year. In contrast, CD8+ T cells, which can control and clear viral infections, can recognise more conserved viral epitopes. Therefore, there is considerable interest in understanding CD8+ T cell responses to influenza virus for the development of future vaccines and therapeutics. Although Alphainfluenzavirus influenzae (FLUAV) and Betainfluenzavirus influenzae (FLUBV) co-circulate in humans and both contribute to seasonal epidemics, there is limited data regarding CD8+ T cell responses to FLUBV. This knowledge gap spans both immunological and molecular insights. In the present review, we summarise the current knowledge of FLUBV-derived CD8+ T cell epitopes at both cellular and molecular levels, in comparison with FLUAV. Collectively, this highlights the limited data available on FLUBV, despite its significant role in human influenza infections.

analysis.scope_and_question: The review examines human seasonal influenza B virus (FLUBV) with a focus on CD8+ T cell responses to conserved epitopes, contrasting with influenza A virus (FLUAV) and addressing the central question of how these responses could inform future vaccines and therapeutics.

analysis.summary_en: This review addresses human seasonal influenza B virus (FLUBV) with a focus on CD8+ T cell responses to conserved epitopes, contrasting with influenza A virus (FLUAV). It highlights that current vaccines, which induce humoral responses against rapidly mutating surface glycoproteins, require annual updates, whereas CD8+ T cells target more conserved epitopes, offering potential for broader protection. The review synthesizes existing knowledge on FLUBV-derived CD8+ T cell epitopes at cellular and molecular levels, explicitly comparing FLUBV to FLUAV. It concludes that CD8+ T cell responses to FLUBV are understudied, with limited data available despite FLUBV's significant role in human influenza infections. The review identifies a critical gap in understanding FLUBV-specific CD8+ T cell epitopes and their HLA class I presentation, emphasizing the need for further research to inform the development of vaccines and therapeutics leveraging conserved T cell responses.

title: Memory B Cell Repertoire of a Repeatedly Vaccinated Individual Includes Influenza Hemagglutinin-Specific Cross-Group Binders with Affinity Beyond A(H1N1)pdm09 and A(H3N2) Seasonal Strains
abstract: Background/Objectives: Humans are primarily infected by two distinct seasonal influenza A virus (IAV) subtypes, A(H1N1)pdm09 and A(H3N2). Because IAV mutates rapidly, it continuously escapes existing protective antibodies. However, repeated exposure to these evolving strains increases the diversity of virus-specific memory B cell (MBC) population. To investigate the extent of this diversity and cross-reactivity of IAV- specific immunity in adults, and its possible impact on emerging strains, we analyzed the hemagglutinin (HA)-specific MBC repertoire of an adult frequently immunized with seasonal vaccines. Methods: High-throughput single-cell sequencing of HA probe-positive MBCs collected from an individual with repeated seasonal influenza vaccination was performed. Monoclonal antibodies (mAbs) from multicell clonotypes were tested for HA binding and influenza virus neutralization. Results: Two clonotypes were identified that bound to both A(H1) and A(H3) HAs from strains circulating before and after the season of blood collection. Both clonotypes neutralized A(H3N2) strains, while one also neutralized A(H1N1)pdm09 strains. Notably, these cross-group binders showed affinity for A(H5), A(H7) and A(H9) avian influenza HAs and neutralized bovine A(H5N1) IAV. Conclusions: Our findings suggest that seasonal vaccination can support pre-existing cross-reactive B-cell immunity in some individuals. This underscores the importance of studying influenza-specific MBC repertoires across diverse populations to better understand immune dynamics and improve vaccine design.

title: Influenza A virus H5N1 genotypes B3.13 and D1.1 show temperature-dependent restriction of replication in primary human respiratory epithelial cell cultures derived from the upper and lower respiratory tract.
abstract: H5N1 clade 2.3.4.4b avian influenza A viruses pose a significant threat to wild animal populations, domesticated animals, and potentially, the human population. For H5N1s to infect and transmit among mammalian species, mutations for improved utilization of mammalian receptors and enhanced replication at the lower temperatures of the upper respiratory tract need to be acquired. A human H1N1pdm09-like virus was compared to H5N1 genotypes B3.13 and D1.1 for replication at 33{o}C, 37{o}C, and 39{o}C - temperatures consistent with the upper and lower respiratory tract in humans, and dairy cow udder tissue. All H5N1 viruses had increased plaque sizes on MDCK cells at 37{o}C and 39{o}C compared to H1N1pdm09. In primary, differentiated human nasal and bronchial epithelial cultures, all H5N1 viruses show restricted infectious virus production compared to H1N1 at 33{o}C. While H5N1 D1.1 also showed restricted replication at 37{o}C and 39{o}C, the H5N1 B3.13 replicated to nearly equivalent titers as H1N1pdm09. All H5N1 viruses demonstrated similar cell tropism in cells from the upper and lower respiratory tract, infecting more ciliated than non-ciliated cells relative to H1N1pdm09. H1N1, H5N1 B3.13 D1.1 infection induced similar innate immune factors, with nasal epithelial cells producing higher levels compared to bronchial epithelial cells. These data suggest that genotype B3.13 and D1.1 H5N1 viruses show different temperature dependent replication patterns compared to H1N1pdm09.

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to investigate the replication characteristics of H5N1 genotypes B3.13 and D1.1 in human respiratory epithelial cell cultures, addressing the knowledge gap about their potential to infect and transmit among mammalian species.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study compared the replication of a human H1N1pdm09-like virus with H5N1 genotypes B3.13 and D1.1 in primary human respiratory epithelial cell cultures derived from both upper and lower respiratory tracts.
analysis.methods: The researchers assessed replication by measuring plaque sizes on MDCK cells at different temperatures (33°C, 37°C, and 39°C) and evaluated infectious virus production in differentiated human nasal and bronchial epithelial cultures.
analysis.main_results: All H5N1 viruses showed increased plaque sizes on MDCK cells at 37°C and 39°C compared to H1N1pdm09. In human respiratory epithelial cultures, H5N1 B3.13 replicated to nearly equivalent titers as H1N1pdm09 at 33°C, while H5N1 D1.1 showed restricted replication at 37°C and 39°C.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The findings suggest that H5N1 genotypes B3.13 and D1.1 exhibit distinct temperature-dependent replication patterns compared to H1N1pdm09, which may have implications for their potential to infect and transmit among mammalian hosts.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The results provide insights into the replication behavior of H5N1 viruses in human respiratory tissues, which could inform surveillance and risk assessment strategies for potential zoonotic transmission.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited to in vitro cell cultures and does not account for in vivo factors, which may affect replication dynamics. The evidence is moderate due to the controlled experimental setting.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigates the replication characteristics of H5N1 genotypes B3.13 and D1.1 in human respiratory epithelial cell cultures. It compares their replication to that of a human H1N1pdm09-like virus at different temperatures, which correspond to the upper and lower respiratory tracts. The results show that H5N1 B3.13 replicates to nearly equivalent titers as H1N1pdm09 at 33°C, while H5N1 D1.1 shows restricted replication at higher temperatures. These findings suggest that the two H5N1 genotypes have different temperature-dependent replication patterns, which may influence their potential to infect and transmit among mammalian species. The study's in vitro setting limits its generalizability, and the evidence is considered moderate due to the controlled experimental environment.

title: An LLM enabled real-time estimation of seasonal influenza vaccine effectiveness from social media data
abstract: Influenza vaccine effectiveness (VE) is estimated from a limited number of clinics using a test-negative design. These standard estimates face geographic, temporal, and operational constraints. Using Twitter/X data, we applied few-shot chain-of-thought prompting to identify self-reported vaccination status and influenza test results, then implemented a test-negative-like design to estimate VE. Our estimates fell within the range of interim reports and could complement current systems, improving feasibility, timeliness, and scalability.

title: Site-specific microRNA responses in lungs of pigs depend on the host-adaptation of H1N1 influenza A virus
abstract: Cross-species transmission of influenza A virus (IAV) represents a major risk for emergence of new pandemics, however, the host molecular responses invoked by cross-species IAV infection remain incompletely defined. MicroRNAs (miRNAs) are important post-transcriptional regulators of innate immunity, but their role during infection with IAV strains of the same subtype but of different host origin has not been investigated. Here, we investigated pulmonary miRNA responses in upper and lower lung sites from pigs inoculated with either a swine-adapted (swH1N1) or a human-adapted (huH1N1) IAV originating from the 2009H1N1 pandemic strain. High-throughput microfluidic RT-qPCR profiling of 115 miRNAs and selected antiviral genes revealed strain-dependent differences, with 33 miRNAs being differentially expressed in pig lungs (upper and lower lung) after human-adapted IAV infection, while only eight miRNAs were altered after swine-adapted IAV infection. Expression of several miRNAs correlated inversely with predicted target pattern recognition receptor (PRR) and interferon-stimulated gene (ISG) transcripts after huH1N1 infection, including miR-19a/b, miR-21-5p, and miR-93-3p, suggesting miRNA-mediated fine-tuning of antiviral signaling. Notably, extensive downregulation of miRNAs in the lower lungs after huH1N1 infection coincided with robust ISG induction, despite huH1N1 viral lung load being comparable to swH1N1 viral load. The swine-adapted IAV, in contrast, triggered stronger RIG-I-like receptor and cGAS transcription without substantial miRNA changes. Together, these findings demonstrate that pulmonary miRNA responses to IAV are both strain- and lung site-specific and may contribute to shaping the outcome of infection depending on the degree of viral host adaptation.

Here, we investigated pulmonary miRNA responses in upper and lower lung sites from pigs inoculated with either a swine-adapted (swH1N1) or a human-adapted (huH1N1) IAV originating from the 2009H1N1 pandemic strain. High-throughput microfluidic RT-qPCR profiling of 115 miRNAs and selected antiviral genes revealed strain-dependent differences, with 33 miRNAs being differentially expressed in pig lungs (upper and lower lung) after human-adapted IAV infection, while only eight miRNAs were altered after swine-adapted IAV infection. Expression of several miRNAs correlated inversely with predicted target pattern recognition receptor (PRR) and interferon-stimulated gene (ISG) transcripts after huH1N1 infection, including miR-19a/b, miR-21-5p, and miR-93-3p, suggesting miRNA-mediated fine-tuning of antiviral signaling. Notably, extensive downregulation of miRNAs in the lower lungs after huH1N1 infection coincided with robust ISG induction, despite huH1N1 viral lung load being comparable to swH1N1 viral load. The swine-adapted IAV, in contrast, triggered stronger RIG-I-like receptor and cGAS transcription without substantial miRNA changes. Together, these findings demonstrate that pulmonary miRNA responses to IAV are both strain- and lung site-specific and may contribute to shaping the outcome of infection depending on the degree of viral host adaptation.

title: Significant upregulation of GSDMD and TfR-1 genes following A/H1N1, A/H3N2, and Flu-B infections
abstract: Influenza viruses, as important respiratory viruses for seasonal flu, are responsible for yearly mortality among human populations. Among different and complex interactions within the cell, pyroptosis and ferroptosis have emerged as two main cell death pathways that are correlated to inflammation following influenza infection. In this study, we have investigated GSDMD (pyroptosis marker) and TfR-1 (ferroptosis marker) mRNA expression, 48 h post-infection (hpi) in A549 infected cells with different types of influenza viruses. A549 cells were infected with A/H1N1, A/H3N2, and Flu-B with 100 TCID50. RNA was extracted by RNJIA RNA extraction kit (RNJIA, ROJE, Iran) 48 hpi, and mRNA expression of GSDMD and TfR-1 was assessed by SYBR Green qRT-PCR. Gene expression data were analyzed using both non-parametric and parametric statistical tests, followed by pairwise post-hoc comparisons. The consistent upregulation of GSDMD and TfR-1 across A/H1N1, A/H3N2, and Flu-B compared to the control groups suggests the involvement of these pro-pyroptotic and pro-ferroptotic factors associated to pyrotposis and ferroptosis cell death pathways following inflammation, 48 hpi. While GSDMD had sharpest upregulation in A/H1N1 compared to A/H3N2 and Flu-B, TfR-1 upregulation showed different pattern with highest upregulation in A/H3N2. In total, our study supports the potential involvement of GSDMD and TfR-1 which are associated with pyroptosis and ferroptosis that are active following different types of influenza viruses.

title_zh: A/H1N1、A/H3N2 和 Flu-B 感染后 GSDMD 和 TfR-1 基因显着上调
source_body_en: Influenza viruses, as important respiratory viruses for seasonal flu, are responsible for yearly mortality among human populations. Among different and complex interactions within the cell, pyroptosis and ferroptosis have emerged as two main cell death pathways that are correlated to inflammation following influenza infection. In this study, we have investigated GSDMD (pyroptosis marker) and TfR-1 (ferroptosis marker) mRNA expression, 48 h post-infection (hpi) in A549 infected cells with different types of influenza viruses. A549 cells were infected with A/H1N1, A/H3N2, and Flu-B with 100 TCID50. RNA was extracted by RNJIA RNA extraction kit (RNJIA, ROJE, Iran) 48 hpi, and mRNA expression of GSDMD and TfR-1 was assessed by SYBR Green qRT-PCR. Gene expression data were analyzed using both non-parametric and parametric statistical tests, followed by pairwise post-hoc comparisons. The consistent upregulation of GSDMD and TfR-1 across A/H1N1, A/H3N2, and Flu-B compared to the control groups suggests the involvement of these pro-pyroptotic and pro-ferroptotic factors associated to pyrotposis and ferroptosis cell death pathways following inflammation, 48 hpi. While GSDMD had sharpest upregulation in A/H1N1 compared to A/H3N2 and Flu-B, TfR-1 upregulation showed different pattern with highest upregulation in A/H3N2. In total, our study supports the potential involvement of GSDMD and TfR-1 which are associated with pyroptosis and ferroptosis that are active following different types of influenza viruses.

title: Neuraminidase and secretory pathway stress converge to remodel host glycosylation during influenza A virus infection
abstract: Abstract Glycosylation is critical for viral-host cell interactions in influenza A virus (IAV) infection, but we lack a comprehensive understanding of how IAV infection shapes the host glycoproteome. Here, we performed liquid chromatography-tandem mass spectrometry (LC-MS/MS) proteomic, glycomic, and glycoproteomic characterisation of the dynamic subcellular responses to an in vitro time course infection of human A549 cells. IAV infection resulted in only modest changes to the subcellular proteome, but robust and significant changes to the host secreted and organelle glycome and glycoproteome. Infection caused reductions in sialylation across the N- and O-glyco(proteo)me; increased oligomannose, paucimannose, and phosphorylated glycans; and shorter hybrid/complex glycans. Desialylation was greater when glycans were fucosylated; for sialic acid linked α2,3 or on the α3 arm; on larger, complex glycans; and on proteins likely to be more accessible to IAV neuraminidase (NA). Subtle activation of the unfolded protein response in infection was associated with a doubling of oligomannose N-glycosylation. Glycans were shorter in infection, implicating IAV-induced disruption of Golgi glycoprotein flux as a mechanism that reduces host glycoprotein sialylation and promotes virion release, independent of NA activity.

analysis.summary_en: This study explores how influenza A virus (IAV) infection alters host glycosylation patterns, revealing significant changes in the secreted and organelle glycome and glycoproteome. Using an in vitro time course infection model of human A549 cells, the researchers observed reductions in sialylation, increases in specific glycans, and shorter hybrid/complex glycans. They also noted a subtle activation of the unfolded protein response associated with increased oligomannose N-glycosylation. These results offer a novel mechanism for IAV replication and could inform future therapeutic strategies. However, the study's reliance on in vitro models and lack of direct functional validation limit the confidence in its conclusions, resulting in a moderate assessment of evidence strength.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 本研究旨在探究甲型流感病毒(IAV)感染如何改变宿主糖蛋白组,因糖基化对病毒-宿主相互作用至关重要,但其机制仍不甚明确。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 该研究使用人类 A549 细胞的体外时程感染模型,采用液相色谱-串联质谱 (LC-MS/MS) 来表征 IAV 感染期间的蛋白质组、糖组和糖蛋白质组变化。
elements_zh.methods: 研究人员进行了 LC-MS/MS 蛋白质组、糖组和糖蛋白质组分析,以检查 IAV 感染的动态亚细胞反应,重点关注聚糖结构的变化及其与 宿主 细胞过程的关联。
elements_zh.main_results: IAV 感染导致 N- 和 O- 糖(蛋白质)组唾液酸化减少,寡甘露糖、寡甘露糖和磷酸化聚糖以及较短的杂合/复合聚糖增加。未折叠蛋白反应的微妙激活与寡甘露糖 N-糖基化的加倍有关。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 研究结果表明,IAV 诱导的高尔基体糖蛋白流的破坏减少了 宿主 糖蛋白唾液酸化,并促进病毒颗粒释放,与神经氨酸酶活性无关,为病毒复制提供了一种新机制。

analysis_en.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to investigate how influenza A virus (IAV) infection alters the host glycoproteome, as glycosylation is essential for viral-host interactions but the mechanisms remain poorly understood.
analysis_en.study_design_and_population: The study used an in vitro time course infection model of human A549 cells, employing liquid chromatography-tandem mass spectrometry (LC-MS/MS) to characterise proteomic, glycomic, and glycoproteomic changes during IAV infection.
analysis_en.methods: The researchers conducted LC-MS/MS proteomic, glycomic, and glycoproteomic analyses to examine the dynamic subcellular responses to IAV infection, focusing on changes in glycan structures and their association with host cell processes.
analysis_en.main_results: IAV infection led to reductions in sialylation across N- and O-glyco(proteo)me, increases in oligomannose, paucimannose, and phosphorylated glycans, and shorter hybrid/complex glycans. analysis_en.interpretation_and_novelty: The findings suggest that IAV-induced disruption of Golgi glycoprotein flux reduces host glycoprotein sialylation and facilitates virion release, independent of neuraminidase activity, offering a novel mechanism for viral replication.
analysis_en.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: These results provide insights into the molecular mechanisms of IAV infection, which could inform the development of targeted therapies and improve understanding of host-virus interactions in seasonal influenza.
analysis_en.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited to in vitro models, which may not fully represent in vivo conditions, and the evidence is based on proteomic and glycomic analyses without direct functional validation, resulting in moderate confidence.

title_zh: 甲型流感病毒感染期间神经氨酸酶和分泌途径应激汇聚重塑 宿主 糖基化
source_body_en: Abstract Glycosylation is critical for viral-host cell interactions in influenza A virus (IAV) infection, but we lack a comprehensive understanding of how IAV infection shapes the host glycoproteome. Here, we performed liquid chromatography-tandem mass spectrometry (LC-MS/MS) proteomic, glycomic, and glycoproteomic characterisation of the dynamic subcellular responses to an in vitro time course infection of human A549 cells. IAV infection resulted in only modest changes to the subcellular proteome, but robust and significant changes to the host secreted and organelle glycome and glycoproteome. Infection caused reductions in sialylation across the N- and O-glyco(proteo)me; increased oligomannose, paucimannose, and phosphorylated glycans; and shorter hybrid/complex glycans. Desialylation was greater when glycans were fucosylated; for sialic acid linked α2,3 or on the α3 arm; on larger, complex glycans; and on proteins likely to be more accessible to IAV neuraminidase (NA). Subtle activation of the unfolded protein response in infection was associated with a doubling of oligomannose N-glycosylation. Glycans were shorter in infection, implicating IAV-induced disruption of Golgi glycoprotein flux as a mechanism that reduces host glycoprotein sialylation and promotes virion release, independent of NA activity.
abstract_zh: 摘要 糖基化对于甲型流感病毒 (IAV) 感染中病毒与 宿主 细胞相互作用至关重要,但我们对 IAV 感染如何塑造 宿主 糖蛋白组缺乏全面的了解。在这里,我们对人 A549 细胞体外时程感染的动态亚细胞反应进行了液相色谱-串联质谱 (LC-MS/MS) 蛋白质组、糖组和糖蛋白质组表征。IAV 感染仅导致亚细胞蛋白质组发生适度变化,但导致 宿主 分泌的细胞器糖组和糖蛋白质组发生强烈且显着的变化。感染导致 N- 和 O-糖(蛋白质)组唾液酸化减少;增加寡甘露糖、寡甘露糖和磷酸化聚糖;和较短的杂合/复合聚糖。当聚糖被岩藻糖基化时,去唾液酸作用更强;对于连接α2,3或α3臂上的唾液酸;较大、复杂的聚糖;以及 IAV 神经氨酸酶 (NA) 更容易接触的蛋白质。感染中未折叠蛋白反应的微妙激活与寡甘露糖 N-糖基化的加倍有关。感染中的聚糖较短,表明 IAV 诱导的高尔基体糖蛋白通量破坏是一种减少 宿主 糖蛋白唾液酸化并促进病毒颗粒释放的机制,与 NA 活性无关。

title: Pre-existing systemic and nasal antibodies against avian H5 influenza A viruses vary according to childhood imprinting
abstract: Avian influenza A viruses (IAVs) pose a constant pandemic threat, with the recent 2.3.4.4b clade of the H5 subtype causing high pathogenicity and spreading across animal species and geographic locations. Understanding human pre-existing immunity to avian H5 IAV can inform on population susceptibility, a critical aspect of pandemic preparedness. To that end, we analyzed the IAV HA-specific antibodies across individuals born between 1928 and 1999 with different early life exposures to IAV subtypes. Individuals born prior to 1957 had the highest pre-existing serum antibodies to group 1 HA antigens, including the 2.3.4.4b H5 and a group 1 HA stem antigen. These birth year-specific patterns were not reflected in the limited pre-existing serum neutralizing antibodies detectable against a 2.3.4.4b H5 IAV or in H5-specific memory B cell populations. They were, however, evident in pre-existing nasal IgG and IgA titers to H5, which were greater in individuals born prior to 1957. Our findings demonstrate that the immunological biases afforded by early life exposure extend to antibodies detected in the nasal mucosa, the site of IAV replication.IMPORTANCEUnderstating pre-existing immunity to influenza A viruses (IAVs) of pandemic potential is an important aspect of pandemic preparedness. This includes an understanding of the heterogeneity of pre-existing immunity across the population. Here, we demonstrate that pre-existing antibodies to H5 IAV vary according to the year of birth and childhood imprinting. We demonstrate that this is the case for both systemic and nasal antibodies, highlighting the importance of understanding pre-existing mucosal immunity at the sites of influenza virus replication.

analysis.research_question_and_background: Avian influenza A viruses (IAVs) pose a pandemic threat, and understanding human pre-existing immunity to avian H5 IAV is critical for pandemic preparedness. The study aimed to determine whether pre-existing antibodies to H5 IAV vary according to childhood imprinting and early life exposure to IAV subtypes.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study analyzed IAV HA-specific antibodies in individuals born between 1928 and 1999, stratified by birth year to reflect different early life exposures to IAV subtypes. Participants were selected to examine systemic and nasal antibody responses to H5 IAV.
analysis.methods: Serum and nasal samples were analyzed for HA-specific antibodies, including serum neutralizing antibodies, memory B cell populations, and nasal IgG and IgA titers against H5 IAV. Antibody levels were measured to assess pre-existing immunity.
analysis.main_results: Individuals born prior to 1957 exhibited the highest pre-existing serum antibodies to group 1 HA antigens, including H5 and a group 1 HA stem antigen. However, these birth year-specific patterns were not reflected in serum neutralizing antibodies against H5 IAV or H5-specific memory B cell populations. Pre-existing nasal IgG and IgA titers to H5 were greater in individuals born prior to 1957.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The findings demonstrate that immunological biases from early life exposure extend to antibodies detected in the nasal mucosa, the primary site of IAV replication. This highlights the importance of understanding mucosal immunity in pandemic preparedness.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The study suggests that childhood imprinting influences pre-existing mucosal immunity to H5 IAV, which may inform surveillance strategies and vaccine design targeting pandemic threats.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited by its focus on pre-existing antibodies and does not address functional immunity or protection against infection. The evidence is moderate, as it relies on cross-sectional sampling and does not establish causality.

analysis.summary_en: This study examined pre-existing antibodies to avian H5 influenza A virus (IAV) in humans, stratified by birth year to reflect early life exposure to IAV subtypes. Individuals born before 1957 showed higher serum antibodies to group 1 HA antigens, including H5, but this pattern did not extend to serum neutralizing antibodies or H5-specific memory B cells. Notably, nasal IgG and IgA titers to H5 were elevated in this group, indicating that childhood imprinting influences mucosal immunity at the site of IAV replication. The findings underscore the importance of understanding mucosal antibody responses for pandemic preparedness, particularly for avian H5 IAV. However, the study is limited by its cross-sectional design and lack of functional immunity assessment, warranting cautious interpretation.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 甲型禽流感病毒 (IAV) 构成大流行威胁,了解人类对禽 H5 IAV 已有的免疫力对于预防大流行至关重要。该研究旨在确定预先存在的 H5 IAV 抗体是否会根据童年印记和早年接触 IAV 亚型而变化。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 该研究分析了 1928 年至 1999 年间出生的个体的 IAV HA 特异性抗体,并按出生年份分层,以反映不同的早期 IAV 亚型暴露情况。选择参与者来检查对 H5 IAV 的全身和鼻腔抗体反应。
elements_zh.methods: 分析血清和鼻腔样本中的 HA 特异性抗体,包括血清中和抗体、记忆 B 细胞群以及针对 H5 IAV 的鼻腔 IgG 和 IgA 滴度。测量抗体水平以评估预先存在的免疫力。
elements_zh.main_results: 1957 年之前出生的个体表现出针对第 1 组 HA 抗原(包括 H5 和第 1 组 HA 干抗原)的最高现有血清抗体。然而,这些出生年份特异性模式并未反映在针对 H5 IAV 或 H5 特异性记忆 B 细胞群的血清中和抗体中。1957 年之前出生的个体中预先存在的 H5 鼻腔 IgG 和 IgA 滴度更高。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 研究结果表明,生命早期接触造成的免疫偏差延伸到鼻粘膜(IAV 复制的主要部位)中检测到的抗体。这凸显了了解粘膜免疫在大流行防范中的重要性。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 该研究表明,童年印记影响预先存在的对 H5 IAV 的粘膜免疫,这可能为针对大流行威胁的 监测 策略和 疫苗 设计提供信息。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该研究的局限性在于其关注的是预先存在的抗体,并且没有涉及功能性免疫或针对感染的保护。证据是中等的,因为它依赖于横截面抽样并且没有建立因果关系。

source_body_en: Avian influenza A viruses (IAVs) pose a constant pandemic threat, with the recent 2.3.4.4b clade of the H5 subtype causing high pathogenicity and spreading across animal species and geographic locations. Understanding human pre-existing immunity to avian H5 IAV can inform on population susceptibility, a critical aspect of pandemic preparedness. To that end, we analyzed the IAV HA-specific antibodies across individuals born between 1928 and 1999 with different early life exposures to IAV subtypes. Individuals born prior to 1957 had the highest pre-existing serum antibodies to group 1 HA antigens, including the 2.3.4.4b H5 and a group 1 HA stem antigen. These birth year-specific patterns were not reflected in the limited pre-existing serum neutralizing antibodies detectable against a 2.3.4.4b H5 IAV or in H5-specific memory B cell populations. They were, however, evident in pre-existing nasal IgG and IgA titers to H5, which were greater in individuals born prior to 1957. Our findings demonstrate that the immunological biases afforded by early life exposure extend to antibodies detected in the nasal mucosa, the site of IAV replication.IMPORTANCEUnderstating pre-existing immunity to influenza A viruses (IAVs) of pandemic potential is an important aspect of pandemic preparedness. This includes an understanding of the heterogeneity of pre-existing immunity across the population. Here, we demonstrate that pre-existing antibodies to H5 IAV vary according to the year of birth and childhood imprinting. We demonstrate that this is the case for both systemic and nasal antibodies, highlighting the importance of understanding pre-existing mucosal immunity at the sites of influenza virus replication.

title: Some Exposure for Influenza Hemagglutinin Interface Antibodies.
abstract: ABSTRACT Influenza viruses are a constant threat to human health. Current vaccines often confer low to moderate protection against infection with seasonal viruses and little‐to‐no protection against pandemic viruses. Improved vaccines are needed. These vaccines will need to reliably elicit antibodies to conserved sites that are broadly protective. One strategy to do so is to design immunogens that present epitopes that are targeted by antibodies that are genetically similar, that humans have the genetic capacity to produce, and that are likely present in human naive B cell repertoires. Among the more recently described epitopes for broadly binding, protective antibodies are those on surfaces at protein–protein interfaces. This review will focus on describing many of these sites and the genetic features of antibodies that engage them. Interface epitopes are immunogenic, and antibodies to these sites are likely present in human repertoires following influenza infection or vaccination.

title_zh: 流感血凝素界面抗体的一些暴露。
source_body_en: ABSTRACT Influenza viruses are a constant threat to human health. Current vaccines often confer low to moderate protection against infection with seasonal viruses and little‐to‐no protection against pandemic viruses. Improved vaccines are needed. These vaccines will need to reliably elicit antibodies to conserved sites that are broadly protective. One strategy to do so is to design immunogens that present epitopes that are targeted by antibodies that are genetically similar, that humans have the genetic capacity to produce, and that are likely present in human naive B cell repertoires. Among the more recently described epitopes for broadly binding, protective antibodies are those on surfaces at protein–protein interfaces. This review will focus on describing many of these sites and the genetic features of antibodies that engage them. Interface epitopes are immunogenic, and antibodies to these sites are likely present in human repertoires following influenza infection or vaccination.

title: Myth-busting influenza and fear of adverse reactions in healthcare workers: two experimental studies on vaccination intentions.
abstract: Background Seasonal influenza causes significant global harms, and vaccinating healthcare workers (HCW) is central to protecting both staff and patients. However, HCW influenza vaccination rates remain below targets. Misconceptions, particularly concerns about adverse reactions, are frequently cited barriers, and many campaigns use myth-busting materials to counter these beliefs. This study tested whether correcting influenza myths and addressing concerns about adverse reactions leads to an increase in vaccine intentions. Methods Two online experimental studies were conducted. HCW participants were of primary interest but a general population sample was included for comparison. In Experiment 1 (HCW n = 514; general population n = 401), participants viewed images debunking common influenza myths, with randomisation to materials that either included or excluded an additional image addressing adverse reactions. Experiment 2 (HCW n = 535; general population n = 1200) focused exclusively on adverse reaction messaging, with participants randomised to one of four image formats. Vaccination intention was the primary outcome. Results In Experiment 1, myth-busting significantly increased vaccination intentions (all p 0.12) in both samples. Adding an adverse reactions image produced no additional increase. In Experiment 2, no overall effects emerged for HCW, but a significant interaction ( p = .011, ηp 2 = 0.04) indicated that effects varied by image: one increased intentions ( p = .029, d z = 0.25), two showed null effects, and one produced a marginal backfire effect ( p = .052 d z = −0.21). In the general population sample, intentions increased overall ( p < .001, d z = 0.15) with no interaction. Conclusions Vaccination intentions were reliably higher after viewing myth-busting materials than before, but control intentions were not. Myth-busting is therefore an effective approach to increasing influenza vaccination intentions. In contrast, explicitly addressing mild adverse reactions did not reliably raise intentions and, for one set of materials, marginally reduced them. Campaigns targeting HCW should therefore test adverse reaction messaging before implementation.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigated the effectiveness of myth-busting materials in increasing influenza vaccination intentions among healthcare workers (HCW) and the general population. Two online experimental studies were conducted, with Experiment 1 testing myth-busting materials that included or excluded adverse reaction images, and Experiment 2 focusing solely on adverse reaction messaging. Results showed that myth-busting significantly increased vaccination intentions in both groups, while addressing adverse reactions had mixed effects. The study suggests that myth-busting is an effective strategy for improving vaccination intentions, but adverse reaction messaging should be tested before implementation. The findings have implications for public health campaigns aimed at increasing vaccine uptake, particularly among HCW.

title_zh: 打破流感神话和医护人员对不良反应的恐惧:关于 疫苗接种 意图的两项实验研究。
source_body_en: Background Seasonal influenza causes significant global harms, and vaccinating healthcare workers (HCW) is central to protecting both staff and patients. However, HCW influenza vaccination rates remain below targets. Misconceptions, particularly concerns about adverse reactions, are frequently cited barriers, and many campaigns use myth-busting materials to counter these beliefs. This study tested whether correcting influenza myths and addressing concerns about adverse reactions leads to an increase in vaccine intentions. Methods Two online experimental studies were conducted. HCW participants were of primary interest but a general population sample was included for comparison. In Experiment 1 (HCW n = 514; general population n = 401), participants viewed images debunking common influenza myths, with randomisation to materials that either included or excluded an additional image addressing adverse reactions. Experiment 2 (HCW n = 535; general population n = 1200) focused exclusively on adverse reaction messaging, with participants randomised to one of four image formats. Vaccination intention was the primary outcome. Results In Experiment 1, myth-busting significantly increased vaccination intentions (all p 0.12) in both samples. Adding an adverse reactions image produced no additional increase. In Experiment 2, no overall effects emerged for HCW, but a significant interaction ( p = .011, ηp 2 = 0.04) indicated that effects varied by image: one increased intentions ( p = .029, d z = 0.25), two showed null effects, and one produced a marginal backfire effect ( p = .052 d z = −0.21). In the general population sample, intentions increased overall ( p < .001, d z = 0.15) with no interaction. Conclusions Vaccination intentions were reliably higher after viewing myth-busting materials than before, but control intentions were not. Myth-busting is therefore an effective approach to increasing influenza vaccination intentions. In contrast, explicitly addressing mild adverse reactions did not reliably raise intentions and, for one set of materials, marginally reduced them. Campaigns targeting HCW should therefore test adverse reaction messaging before implementation.

title: Influenza A H1N1 Infection Triggers Endothelial Immunothrombosis via TNF-α–Tissue Factor–Thrombin Signaling in Human Brain Microvascular Endothelial Cells
abstract: Severe Influenza A virus (IAV) infection is associated with endothelial dysfunction, inflammation, and coagulation abnormalities. However, the mechanisms linking endothelial inflammatory activation to thrombosis remain incompletely understood. We investigated whether Influenza A/H1N1 induces an immunothrombotic phenotype in human brain microvascular endothelial cells. We infected HBEC-5i cells with Influenza A/H1N1 pdm09. We assessed viral infection by RT-qPCR detection of matrix (M) transcripts and by immunoblotting for the M1 protein. We evaluated endothelial responses by measuring TNF-α expression and secretion, Tissue Factor (TF) expression, TF-dependent factor Xa generation, and responses to recombinant TNF-α and thrombin. H1N1 infection increased TNF-α expression and secretion and enhanced TF expression and functional activity, indicating acquisition of a procoagulant endothelial phenotype. Recombinant TNF-α reproduced infection-associated TF induction, whereas thrombin enhanced TNF-α production and TF activity, supporting reciprocal amplification between inflammatory and coagulation pathways. These findings support a TNF-α–TF–thrombin feed-forward signaling circuit linking endothelial inflammation and coagulation during H1N1 infection. Influenza A/H1N1 induces an immunothrombotic phenotype in human brain microvascular endothelial cells, identifying this signaling axis as a potential mechanistic target for influenza-associated vascular and thrombotic complications.

title_zh: 甲型 H1N1 流感感染通过人脑微血管内皮细胞中的 TNF-α-组织因子-凝血酶信号触发内皮免疫血栓形成
source_body_en: Severe Influenza A virus (IAV) infection is associated with endothelial dysfunction, inflammation, and coagulation abnormalities. However, the mechanisms linking endothelial inflammatory activation to thrombosis remain incompletely understood. We investigated whether Influenza A/H1N1 induces an immunothrombotic phenotype in human brain microvascular endothelial cells. We infected HBEC-5i cells with Influenza A/H1N1 pdm09. We assessed viral infection by RT-qPCR detection of matrix (M) transcripts and by immunoblotting for the M1 protein. We evaluated endothelial responses by measuring TNF-α expression and secretion, Tissue Factor (TF) expression, TF-dependent factor Xa generation, and responses to recombinant TNF-α and thrombin. H1N1 infection increased TNF-α expression and secretion and enhanced TF expression and functional activity, indicating acquisition of a procoagulant endothelial phenotype. Recombinant TNF-α reproduced infection-associated TF induction, whereas thrombin enhanced TNF-α production and TF activity, supporting reciprocal amplification between inflammatory and coagulation pathways. These findings support a TNF-α–TF–thrombin feed-forward signaling circuit linking endothelial inflammation and coagulation during H1N1 infection. Influenza A/H1N1 induces an immunothrombotic phenotype in human brain microvascular endothelial cells, identifying this signaling axis as a potential mechanistic target for influenza-associated vascular and thrombotic complications.

title: Clinical and public health economic impact of rapid strain-matched vaccination in influenza pandemic mitigation: A UK-like population dynamic transmission model
abstract: Influenza A virus H5N1 has recently circulated at unprecedented levels in birds and mammals, causing sporadic human infections. Using a susceptible-exposed-infectious-recovered (SEIR) dynamic transmission model of a UK-like population, this study aimed to quantify reductions in morbidity, mortality, and healthcare utilization attributable to rapid deployment of a strain-matched pandemic influenza vaccine; to compare outcomes across egg-based and cell-based vaccine platforms; to evaluate the economic impact of nonpharmaceutical interventions (NPIs) and their interaction with vaccination timing; and to estimate the impact of earlier or delayed vaccine availability across a full spectrum of pandemic transmissibility and severity scenarios. In the absence of NPIs, a 16-week vaccination campaign starting 16 weeks post-pandemic declaration reduced infections by 3.0 million and deaths by 28,000, with greater benefits observed in low-transmissibility scenarios. A cell-based vaccine with equivalent timing further reduced deaths by 5.0%, with additional gains in scenarios involving faster vaccine production. NPIs (average cost, £208 billion) enhanced vaccine effectiveness across all pandemic types, most markedly in high-transmissibility events; cell-based vaccine additionally reduced NPI costs by 0.9% relative to egg-based vaccine. Conversely, delays in vaccine availability increased both mortality and economic costs. These findings highlight the need for robust and agile vaccine development, registration, and distribution infrastructures, as well as flexible response strategies adaptable to varying pandemic severity and transmissibility. Policymakers should consider adopting a comprehensive framework integrating health outcome metrics and the economic impact of NPIs to inform vaccine procurement and deployment decisions.

elements_zh.methods: 该研究采用 SEIR 模型来模拟大流行性流感动态,结合不同的 疫苗 平台(基于鸡蛋和基于细胞),并评估非药物干预措施 (NPI) 以及 疫苗接种 时机和可用性的经济影响。
elements_zh.main_results: A 16-week vaccination campaign starting 16 weeks post-pandemic declaration reduced infections by 3.0 million and deaths by 28,000, with greater benefits observed in low-transmissibility scenarios. Delays in vaccine availability increased both mortality and economic costs.
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 研究结果表明,快速菌株匹配的 疫苗接种 显着减少了感染和死亡,特别是在低传播率的情况下,并且 疫苗 可用性的延迟会对健康结果和经济成本产生不利影响。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 结果表明及时部署 疫苗 的重要性,并强调需要采取灵活的策略来应对不同的流行病严重程度和传播性,并对公共卫生规划和资源分配产生影响。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该研究依赖于基于模型的方法,可能无法完全捕捉现实世界的复杂性,并且证据基于模拟场景而不是经验数据,导致研究结果的可信度中等。

title: Surveillance without silos: a One Health data imperative for avian influenza in West Africa
abstract: Highly pathogenic avian influenza (HPAI) has circulated in West Africa since Nigeria’s first human case in 2006, making the region a key entry point and dispersal hub for multiple virus lineages in sub-Saharan Africa. The 2.3.4.4b virus clade driving the global spread of avian influenza is now infecting mammals more often, a troubling sign that raises the risk of a future pandemic. At the same time, West Africa’s ability to control HPAI is held back by fragmented surveillance systems. Establishing fully integrated, system-wide national surveillance platforms is indispensable for effective preparedness. Without such integration, West African countries will continue to detect and respond to emerging health threats too late. title: NS-segment-based reporter influenza A viruses: engineering strategy, applications, and limitations
abstract: ABSTRACT Reporter-expressing recombinant influenza A viruses (IAVs) have emerged as powerful tools for studying viral infection, host–pathogen interactions, and the identification and characterization of prophylactic and/or therapeutic countermeasures for the treatment of IAV infections. By incorporating a reporter gene, such as fluorescent, recombinase, or luciferase proteins, into the viral genome, these genetically engineered recombinant IAVs enable real-time visualization and quantification of infection in vitro , ex vivo , and in vivo to detect the presence of IAV in infected cells or animal models of infection. Among the various approaches to express reporter genes from the viral genome, fusion of fluorescent or luciferase proteins to the C-terminus of the non-structural 1 (NS1) protein has been successfully used to generate replication-competent reporter-expressing IAVs. This minireview summarizes the strategies used to generate IAV-expressing reporter genes, particularly from the non-structural (NS) viral segment 8, and their use in real-time tracking of viral replication and pathogenesis. These replication-competent reporter-expressing IAVs also provide an efficient tool for high-throughput screening (HTS) of novel anti-IAV therapeutics. We also discuss the advantages and limitations of current fluorescent and luciferase reporter-expressing IAVs to track viral infections in cultured cells and/or animal models, and provide perspectives on future directions in this rapidly advancing field.

analysis.scope_and_question: The review focuses on the development and use of NS-segment-based reporter influenza A viruses to study viral infection, host–pathogen interactions, and the identification of countermeasures for IAV infections. The target entities include seasonal human influenza A(H1N1)pdm09, A(H3N2), B/Victoria, and B/Yamagata viruses. The central question is about the engineering strategies and applications of these reporter-expressing viruses.
analysis.evidence_base_and_review_method: The review is a minireview that summarizes the strategies used to generate IAV-expressing reporter genes, particularly from the non-structural (NS) viral segment 8. It discusses the incorporation of reporter genes such as fluorescent, recombinase, or luciferase proteins into the viral genome to enable real-time visualization and quantification of infection in vitro, ex vivo, and in vivo. The review does not explicitly report on meta-analysis or consensus process.
analysis.consensus_and_key_conclusions: The review highlights that fusion of fluorescent or luciferase proteins to the C-terminus of the NS1 protein has been successfully used to generate replication-competent reporter-expressing IAVs. These viruses are useful for real-time tracking of viral replication and pathogenesis, and they serve as efficient tools for high-throughput screening of novel anti-IAV therapeutics.
analysis.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: The review notes that while reporter-expressing IAVs are valuable tools, their advantages and limitations are discussed. However, the evidence does not provide specific details on conflicting findings, heterogeneity, or unresolved mechanisms. The review also does not explicitly mention evidence gaps in certain populations or regions.
analysis.research_and_practice_implications: The review suggests that future research should focus on improving the utility of reporter-expressing IAVs for tracking viral infections in cultured cells and animal models. It also emphasizes the need for further exploration of these viruses as tools for high-throughput screening of anti-IAV therapeutics.

title: First detection and molecular characterization of influenza D virus in livestock from Kazakhstan reveals circulation of the D/Yama2019 lineage
abstract: Influenza D virus (IDV) is an emerging Orthomyxovirus primarily associated with cattle and increasingly recognized as a pathogen of veterinary and zoonotic relevance. Despite growing evidence of its circulation across Asia, Europe, and North America, no data have previously been available from Kazakhstan or Central Asia. This study investigated the presence of IDV in domestic livestock samples collected during active surveillance between 2023 and 2026. A total of 867 biological samples were obtained from cattle ( n = 611), camels ( n = 175), Maral Deer ( n = 51), and pigs ( n = 30) across multiple regions of Kazakhstan. title: Highly pathogenic avian influenza viruses in mammals: host-range expansion and implications of milk-borne viral shedding
abstract: SUMMARY Highly pathogenic avian influenza (HPAI) viruses, especially subtype H5N1, have caused major outbreaks in poultry and serious human infections since the first description of “fowl plague” in 1878. Over time, these viruses have expanded their host range, causing huge losses in domestic poultry, spreading among wild bird populations, and occasionally infecting humans. Understanding how influenza viruses adapt and cross species barriers depends on analyzing their fundamental molecular characteristics. Key features such as the polybasic cleavage site within the hemagglutinin protein and the distinctive “1+7” ribonucleoprotein complex, which consists of a single polymerase core surrounded by seven RNA segments, enhance viral replication and broaden host range. Despite decades of intervention, including lessons from the 1997 Hong Kong outbreak and the continued global circulation of clade 2.3.4.4b, HPAI remains difficult to control. A major shift occurred in 2024, when H5N1 was detected in U.S. This was the first confirmed instance of viral shedding into milk from a mammalian host, suggesting a new potential route of transmission beyond the traditional avian reservoirs. This review unites historical milestones, structural insights, epidemiological data, and recent cross-species findings to better define the current landscape of risk and transmission. We further discuss economic, public health, and agricultural impacts of these developments, particularly the 2024 cattle cases, and underscore the urgent need for an integrated One Health approach to better manage the growing risks posed by HPAI viruses.

title: A Novel Cell-Based High-Throughput Screening Model for Inhibitors Targeting Influenza Virus Hemagglutinin–α-2,6-Sialic Acid Interaction
abstract: Rising drug resistance undermines current anti-influenza virus therapies. Although targeting the hemagglutinin (HA)–sialic acid receptor interaction is a promising strategy, progress is impeded by the lack of subtype-independent screening models. Herein, we established a fluorescence-based cell high-throughput model using fluorescein isothiocyanate-conjugated Sambucus Nigra Lectin (FITC-SNA) as a stable HA surrogate and α-2,6-sialyltransferase (ST6GAL1)-overexpressing MDCK cells to mimic the HA–receptor interface. This platform was designed to serve as an efficient primary screening tool to rapidly filter large compound libraries for potential binders to the receptor-binding interface. Screening 10,000 compounds identified Obatoclax Mesylate and Ethylparaben as primary hits. Both exhibited broad-spectrum HA inhibition activity, validating the model’s capability to identify compounds interfering with viral attachment. Further cellular antiviral assays revealed cytotoxicity for both compounds, resulting in low selectivity indexes (SIs), indicating that while these molecules effectively target the interaction site, they require substantial structural optimization for therapeutic use. Molecular docking confirmed their binding to type A H1N1, H3N2, and B/Victoria HA proteins, while ADMET predictions highlighted specific structural optimization needs to mitigate toxicity. In conclusion, this subtype-independent, highly specific high-throughput screening (HTS) model provides an efficient and reliable platform for early-stage influenza drug discovery and lead compound development.

title: Acute viral infection accelerates neurodegeneration in a mouse model of ALS
abstract: Summary While several viral infections have been associated with amyotrophic lateral sclerosis (ALS), the mechanism(s) through which they promote disease has remained almost entirely elusive. This study investigated the impact of common, acute viral infections prior to disease onset on ALS progression in the SOD1 G93A mouse model. A single sublethal infection prior to onset of ALS clinical signs was associated with markedly accelerated ALS disease progression characterized by rapid loss of hindlimb function. Prior infection resulted in gliosis in the lumbar spine and upregulation of transcriptional pathways involved in inflammatory responses, metabolic dysregulation, and muscular dysfunction. Therapeutic suppression of gliosis with an anti-inflammatory small molecule, or administration of a direct-acting antiviral, was associated with significantly improved ALS clinical signs, akin to what was observed in uninfected animals. This study provides causal and mechanistic evidence that the immune response elicited by acute viral infections may be an important etiological factor that alters ALS disease trajectory, and provides insight into novel therapeutic and preventative strategies for ALS. One Sentence Summary Acute viral infection with influenza A virus and SARS-CoV-2 accelerates the progression of ALS in SOD1 G93A mice.

title: Multistability, chaos, and transient dynamics in an avian influenza mathematical model
abstract: Abstract Influenza, commonly known as the flu, is a highly contagious respiratory infection that causes symptoms, such as cough, aches, and malaise in infected individuals. One important form of influenza A infection is avian influenza, caused by the H5N1 virus, which has been a concern since the late twentieth century due to its high mortality rate. Monitoring and controlling avian influenza is of great importance for public health issues due to its ability to infect other mammals and its potential risk for spillover to humans. Mathematical models capable of describing the dynamics of avian influenza have been proposed to explore the spread of the disease and adapt control measures to contain it. In this work, we analyze the dynamical behavior of an avian influenza model consisting of two coupled SI (susceptible-infected) models, one describing the bird population and the other the human population. Using the bird mortality rate as the control parameter and hysteresis-type bifurcation diagrams, we identify bistability over a wide parameter range. As this parameter increases, we observe a significant range of hyperchaos. Furthermore, we uncover and quantify transient chaos and boundary crises for a given set of parameter values. These findings contribute to a more detailed understanding of the non-linear dynamics that may arise in mathematical models of avian influenza transmission.

source_records.title: Multistability, chaos, and transient dynamics in an avian influenza mathematical model
source_records.abstract: Abstract Influenza, commonly known as the flu, is a highly contagious respiratory infection that causes symptoms, such as cough, aches, and malaise in infected individuals. One important form of influenza A infection is avian influenza, caused by the H5N1 virus, which has been a concern since the late twentieth century due to its high mortality rate. Monitoring and controlling avian influenza is of great importance for public health issues due to its ability to infect other mammals and its potential risk for spillover to humans. Mathematical models capable of describing the dynamics of avian influenza have been proposed to explore the spread of the disease and adapt control measures to contain it. In this work, we analyze the dynamical behavior of an avian influenza model consisting of two coupled SI (susceptible-infected) models, one describing the bird population and the other the human population. Using the bird mortality rate as the control parameter and hysteresis-type bifurcation diagrams, we identify bistability over a wide parameter range. As this parameter increases, we observe a significant range of hyperchaos. Furthermore, we uncover and quantify transient chaos and boundary crises for a given set of parameter values. These findings contribute to a more detailed understanding of the non-linear dynamics that may arise in mathematical models of avian influenza transmission.

title: Determinants of highly pathogenic avian influenza spread during bird migration
abstract: Abstract Migratory waterfowl are central to the global spread of the Goose/Guangdong lineage of H5 highly pathogenic avian influenza (HPAI), yet the parameters and processes shaping their role remain poorly understood, with evidence scattered across studies focused on narrow sets of parameters. Here, we synthesized current knowledge to identify 43 parameters and developed a spatially explicit agent-based model of waterfowl migration to evaluate the influence of 28 of these parameters on nine HPAI outcomes. Our results show that migratory waterfowl contribute most to HPAI spread and risk under conditions of high bird-to-bird transmission rate, long infectious periods and greater aggregation of birds at stop-over sites. When aggregation level is held constant, lower overlap in migratory routes among individuals (‘spatial alignment’) further amplifies waterfowl contributions by extending infection maintenance in waterfowl population and the environment. These results suggest that a few viral parameters shape much of infection dynamics, but also that migration behaviour, via aggregation and spatial alignment, plays a comparably large role within our model. Viral traits strongly shaped infection prevalence in waterfowl and incursion risk to poultry, whereas migratory behaviour more strongly shaped outbreak timing, maintenance and spatial distribution. These findings underscore the importance of integrating waterfowl movement ecology into HPAI risk models and assessments.

title: Wastewater and Environmental Surveillance in Cities with Sewered and Non-sewered Sanitation: Evidence from Kampala, Uganda
abstract: Summary Background: Wastewater and environmental surveillance (WES) enables community-level monitoring of infectious diseases. Most progress has focused on sewer-based surveillance, yet nearly half of the global population relies on non-sewered sanitation. In non-sewered settings, urban drainage channels have been used for poliovirus environmental surveillance, but their potential for a multi-pathogen WES with spatially defined catchments, and comparability to sewer-based surveillance, remains under-explored. Methods: Ten drainage channel sampling points with delineated micro-catchments (0.95-3.83 km2 with 12,885-44,146 people) were selected within Kampala. A total of 255 drainage channel and 54 wastewater treatment plant (WWTP) influent samples were collected during two campaigns in March and September-October 2025. A multi-target panel was quantified by digital PCR, including enteric viruses (Norovirus GI and GII, Rotavirus), respiratory viruses (SARS-CoV-2, Influenza A and B viruses, Respiratory Syncytial Virus (RSV)), non-O1/O139 Vibrio cholerae (V. cholerae), and Pepper Mild Mottle Virus (PMMoV) as a fecal indicator. Findings: Enteric viruses, non-O1/O139 V. cholerae, and PMMoV were consistently detected across all drainage channels and WWTP influents. Concentrations were generally lower in drainage than WWTP influents, except for non-O1/O139 V. When normalized by PMMoV, concentrations across most drainage channels were comparable to WWTP influents, although comparability varied by target and location. Both concentrations and PMMoV-normalized concentrations varied across sampling locations. Trends between campaigns varied by pathogen target and were not explained by any single micro-catchment characteristic. Influenza A virus was the most frequently detected respiratory virus (8-23% in drainage channels; 3-10% in WWTP influents), while SARS-CoV-2, Influenza B, and RSV were rarely detected. Interpretation: PMMoV-normalized concentrations across most micro-catchments were comparable to WWTP influents, with spatial heterogeneity implying neighborhood-level differences in disease prevalence. Catchment-delineated drainage surveillance has potential to offer spatially resolved public health information in non-sewered settings comparable to sewer-based wastewater monitoring. Funding: Eawag Discretionary Funding

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to evaluate the potential of urban drainage channels for multi-pathogen wastewater and environmental surveillance in non-sewered settings, addressing the gap in understanding their comparability to sewer-based systems.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study was conducted in Kampala, Uganda, during two campaigns in March and September-October 2025, involving 10 drainage channel sampling points with defined micro-catchments and 255 drainage channel samples alongside 54 wastewater treatment plant influent samples.
analysis.methods: A multi-target panel was quantified using digital PCR, including enteric viruses, respiratory viruses such as influenza A and B, SARS-CoV-2, and RSV, as well as non-O1/O139 Vibrio cholerae and PMMoV as a fecal indicator.
analysis.main_results: Enteric viruses, non-O1/O139 V. cholerae, and PMMoV were consistently detected across all drainage channels and WWTP influents. Influenza A virus was the most frequently detected respiratory virus, with 8-23% in drainage channels and 3-10% in WWTP influents, while SARS-CoV-2, Influenza B, and RSV were rarely detected.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: PMMoV-normalized concentrations across most micro-catchments were comparable to WWTP influents, suggesting that drainage-based surveillance can provide spatially resolved public health information in non-sewered settings.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: Catchment-delineated drainage surveillance has potential to offer spatially resolved public health information in non-sewered settings comparable to sewer-based wastewater monitoring, which could inform targeted interventions.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study's results varied across sampling locations and campaigns, and trends were not explained by any single micro-catchment characteristic, indicating potential limitations in spatial generalizability and the need for further validation.

analysis.summary_en: This study evaluated the feasibility of using urban drainage channels for multi-pathogen wastewater and environmental surveillance in non-sewered settings, comparing them to sewer-based systems. In Kampala, Uganda, 255 drainage channel and 54 wastewater treatment plant influent samples were collected during two campaigns in 2025. A multi-target panel, including enteric and respiratory viruses, was analyzed using digital PCR. Enteric viruses, non-O1/O139 Vibrio cholerae, and PMMoV were consistently detected in both drainage and WWTP samples. Influenza A virus was the most frequently detected respiratory virus, with higher prevalence in drainage channels than in WWTP influents. PMMoV-normalized concentrations across most micro-catchments were comparable to WWTP influents, suggesting that drainage-based surveillance could provide spatially resolved public health data. However, results varied by location and campaign, and no single micro-catchment characteristic explained these trends. The study highlights the potential of drainage surveillance in non-sewered areas but underscores the need for further research to validate its consistency and generalizability.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 该研究旨在评估无下水道环境中城市排水渠道对多病原体废水和环境 监测 的潜力,解决在了解其与基于下水道系统的可比性方面的差距。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 该研究在 2025 年 3 月和 9 月至 10 月的两次活动期间在乌干达坎帕拉进行,涉及 10 个具有明确微集水区的排水沟采样点和 255 个排水沟样品以及 54 个废水 治疗 工厂进水样品。
elements_zh.methods: 使用数字 PCR 对多目标组进行定量,包括肠道病毒、呼吸道病毒(例如甲型和乙型流感)、SARS-CoV-2 和 RSV,以及作为粪便指标的非 O1/O139 霍乱弧菌和 PMMoV。
elements_zh.main_results: 在所有排水渠道和污水处理厂进水中均检测到肠道病毒、非 O1/O139 霍乱弧菌和 PMMoV。甲型流感病毒是最常检测到的呼吸道病毒,在排水沟中占 8-23%,在污水处理厂进水中占 3-10%,而 SARS-CoV-2、乙型流感和 RSV 则很少检测到。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 大多数微流域的 PMMoV 标准化浓度与污水处理厂进水相当,这表明基于排水的 监测 可以在无下水道环境中提供空间解析的公共卫生信息。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 流域划定的排水 监测 有潜力在无下水道环境中提供空间解析的公共卫生信息,与基于下水道的废水监测相当,这可以为有针对性的干预措施提供信息。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该研究的结果因采样地点和活动的不同而有所不同,并且趋势不能用任何单一的微流域特征来解释,这表明空间普遍性的潜在局限性以及需要进一步验证。

abstract_zh: 研究背景:污水与环境监测(WES)可用于社区层面的传染病监测。目前大部分进展集中于基于污水管网的监测,但全球近一半人口依赖无污水管网的卫生设施。在无污水管网的环境中,城市排水渠道已被用于脊髓灰质炎病毒的环境监测,但其在多病原体WES中的潜力、空间定义的汇水区域以及与基于污水管网的监测的可比性仍有待探索。方法:在坎帕拉市内选择了10个排水渠道采样点,并划定了微汇水区域(0.95-3.83 km2,覆盖12,885-44,146人)。在2025年3月及9-10月的两次采样活动中,共收集了255份排水渠道样本和54份污水处理厂(WWTP)进水样本。通过数字PCR定量检测多靶标面板,包括肠道病毒(诺如病毒GI和GII、轮状病毒)、呼吸道病毒(SARS-CoV-2、甲型和乙型流感病毒、呼吸道合胞病毒(RSV))、非O1/O139霍乱弧菌(V. cholerae)以及作为粪便指示剂的辣椒轻斑驳病毒(PMMoV)。研究结果:肠道病毒、非O1/O139霍乱弧菌和PMMoV在所有排水渠道及WWTP进水样本中均被持续检出。除非O1/O139霍乱弧菌外,排水渠道中的浓度通常低于WWTP进水样本。在以PMMoV标准化后,大多数排水渠道的浓度与WWTP进水样本相当,但不同靶标和地点的可比性存在差异。浓度及PMMoV标准化后的浓度在采样点间存在空间变异。两次采样活动的趋势因病原体靶标而异,且无法用单一微汇水区域特征解释。甲型流感病毒是最常检出的呼吸道病毒(排水渠道中占8-23%,WWTP进水中占3-10%),而SARS-CoV-2、乙型流感病毒和RSV的检出率较低。结论:大多数微汇水区域的PMMoV标准化浓度与WWTP进水样本相当,空间异质性表明疾病患病率在社区层面存在差异。划定汇水区域的排水渠道监测有潜力在无污水管网环境中提供与基于污水管网的废水监测相当的空间分辨率公共卫生信息。资助:Eawag自主资金
