analysis_zh.research_question_and_background: 该研究旨在评估无下水道环境中城市排水渠道对多病原体废水和环境 监测 的潜力,解决在了解其与基于下水道系统的可比性方面的差距。
analysis_zh.study_design_and_population: 该研究在 2025 年 3 月和 9 月至 10 月的两次活动期间在乌干达坎帕拉进行,涉及 10 个具有明确微集水区的排水沟采样点和 255 个排水沟样品以及 54 个废水 治疗 工厂进水样品。
analysis_zh.methods: 使用数字 PCR 对多目标组进行定量,包括肠道病毒、呼吸道病毒(例如甲型和乙型流感)、SARS-CoV-2 和 RSV,以及作为粪便指标的非 O1/O139 霍乱弧菌和 PMMoV。
analysis_zh.main_results: 在所有排水渠道和污水处理厂进水中均检测到肠道病毒、非 O1/O139 霍乱弧菌和 PMMoV。甲型流感病毒是最常检测到的呼吸道病毒,在排水沟中占 8-23%,在污水处理厂进水中占 3-10%,而 SARS-CoV-2、乙型流感和 RSV 则很少检测到。
analysis_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 大多数微流域的 PMMoV 标准化浓度与污水处理厂进水相当,这表明基于排水的 监测 可以在无下水道环境中提供空间解析的公共卫生信息。
analysis_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 流域划定的排水 监测 有潜力在无下水道环境中提供空间解析的公共卫生信息,与基于下水道的废水监测相当,这可以为有针对性的干预措施提供信息。
analysis_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该研究的结果因采样地点和活动的不同而有所不同,并且趋势不能用任何单一的微流域特征来解释,这表明空间普遍性的潜在局限性以及需要进一步验证。

title: Exploring integrated advice and avian influenza knowledge gaps by using a Highly Pathogenic Avian Influenza outbreak simulation
abstract: Background Initial evaluations of the COVID-19 pandemic suggested that broad multidisciplinary expertise is needed for an all of society pandemic response. However, it is unclear whether balanced, multi-perspective scientific advising is secured in separate disciplinary advisory committees. Aim Our aim was to explore the potential of integrated advising among biomedical, societal and economic experts into pandemic response, using a simulation of a highly pathogenic avian influenza (HPAI) outbreak. Additionally, we aimed to identify cross-cutting gaps in knowledge and expertise relevant for HPAI pandemic preparedness. Methods We conducted two table-top simulation exercises (April/May 2024), based on a fictitious HPAI outbreak originating in the Netherlands and associated with severe disease among children. In total, 22 and 19 experts participated, representing biomedical, societal and economic sciences. Participants first drafted an outbreak management advice in separate biomedical and societal teams, followed by integrated deliberations and advice in mixed groups. Written notes of the deliberations and pre-simulation interviews was used for an inductive, reflexive thematic analysis. Results Separate advisory processes differed in perceived urgency, situation assessment, and the drafted best- and worst-case scenarios. Mixed groups deliberations exposed disciplinary blind spots and fostered mutual understanding. In particular, school closure was discussed extensively due to conflicting perspectives. Cross-cutting knowledge and know-how gaps were identified in the alignment of (infra)structures and guidelines. Conclusions Our simulation exercises suggest that an integrated advisory approach may have an added value in overcoming conflicting advice during pandemics. Further research is needed to explore whether this observed added value extends to an integrated advisory body.

title: H5N1 influenza multi-epitope vaccine design through immunoinformatics approaches
abstract: The H5N1 avian influenza virus poses a significant threat to both animal and human health, with a high potential for triggering a global pandemic. This study outlines a step-by-step immunoinformatics-driven approach to design a multi-epitope vaccine against H5N1. Potential vaccine candidates were identified by analyzing the sequences of conserved H5N1 proteins, including Hemagglutinin, Neuraminidase, and Matrix protein 1 and 2. B-cell epitopes and T-cell peptides were predicted and then screened for toxicity and allergenicity. The final vaccine construct has been verified for structural stability and computer simulation has been used to evaluate its theoretical potential for eliciting a long-lasting immune response. This In silico approach leverages a suite of computational tools to accelerate vaccine design by prioritizing promising candidates for experimental validation.
journal: Frontiers in Applied Mathematics and Statistics

title: Highly persistent antibody levels but limited population immunity in gannets after HPAI outbreak
abstract: Abstract The recent large-scale circulation of High Pathogenicity Avian Influenza (HP AI) viruses H5Nx of clade 2.3.4.4b has been responsible for massive die-offs in wild species, notably in long-lived seabirds, with unknown implications for the immunity of surviving individuals. In the North Atlantic, northern gannet colonies were heavily affected in 2022, with more than 40% mortality observed among breeding adults and some surviving individuals developing dark irises. Using samples collected in 2023 and 2024 on Rouzic colony (France), we report persistent individual anti-AI antibody levels and seroneutralisation titres, with most of the immune individuals showing dark irises. A modelling approach further stressed the importance of long-lasting immunity in such species by showing that the proportion of individuals which kept their immunity between years strongly limited decreases in population size in case of repeated outbreaks. Overall, our results highlight the existence and importance of long-lasting immunity in long-lived species for population persistence.

title: Beyond Viral Load: A Mechanistic Model of Virus-Immune Dynamics and Age-Dependent Influenza Severity
abstract: Influenza infection results from tightly coupled interactions between viral replication, host immune responses, and the emergence of clinical symptoms. While mathematical models have extensively characterized viral and immune dynamics, the mechanistic link between immune activity and disease severity remains poorly understood. Here, we develop an integrative, within-host modeling framework that explicitly connects infection dynamics, immune responses, and symptom manifestation through a unified dynamical system. Using murine influenza data, we incorporate key immune components alongside a mechanistic representation of symptom progression, quantified via host weight loss.Our analysis identifies inflammatory signaling, particularly TNF- mediated pathways, as a central driver linking immune activity to symptom severity. Importantly, we demonstrate that age-dependent alterations in immune regulation reshape this coupling: aged hosts exhibit prolonged inflammatory responses that amplify and sustain symptom burden despite comparable viral kinetics. These results highlight that disease severity cannot be inferred from viral load alone, but instead emerges from the dynamical interplay between immune regulation and host physiology. This framework provides a quantitative basis for understanding age-specific morbidity and offers a foundation for designing interventions that target immune-mediated pathology rather than viral replication alone.

elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 作者开发了一个综合的 宿主 内建模框架,将感染动态、免疫应答 和症状进展联系起来。该研究使用鼠流感数据来量化 宿主 体重减轻,作为症状严重程度的衡量标准。
elements_zh.methods: 该框架整合了关键的免疫成分和症状进展的机制表示,其中炎症信号传导(尤其是 TNF 介导的途径)被认为是将免疫活动与症状严重程度联系起来的核心。该模型通过统一的动力系统明确地将病毒复制、免疫应答 和临床症状联系起来。
elements_zh.main_results: 分析表明,炎症信号传导,尤其是 TNF 介导的途径,驱动免疫活动与症状严重程度之间的耦合。尽管病毒动力学相当,但老年 宿主 表现出长时间的炎症反应,从而放大并维持症状负担。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 作者将这些发现解释为证明疾病的严重程度不能仅从病毒载量来推断,而是从免疫调节和 宿主 生理学之间的动态相互作用中得出。新颖之处在于通过机制模型将免疫介导的病理学与症状表现明确联系起来。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 该框架为了解流感的年龄特异性发病率提供了定量基础,并表明针对免疫介导的病理学而不是病毒复制的干预措施可能更有效地降低疾病的严重程度。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 证据仅限于小鼠数据和仅摘要的报告,这限制了对人类群体的普遍适用性。由于依赖单一模型生物且缺乏人类验证,证据的强度中等。

abstract_zh: 流感感染是由病毒复制、宿主 免疫应答 和临床症状的出现之间紧密耦合的相互作用引起的。虽然数学模型已经广泛描述了病毒和免疫动力学的特征,但免疫活动和疾病严重程度之间的机制联系仍然知之甚少。在这里,我们开发了一个综合的 宿主 内建模框架,该框架通过统一的动力系统明确连接感染动态、免疫应答 和症状表现。使用鼠流感数据,我们将关键的免疫成分与症状进展的机制表示结合起来,通过 宿主 体重减轻进行量化。我们的分析确定了炎症信号传导,特别是 TNF 介导的途径,作为将免疫活动与症状严重程度联系起来的中心驱动因素。重要的是,我们证明,年龄依赖性的免疫调节改变重塑了这种耦合:尽管病毒动力学相当,但衰老的 宿主 表现出延长的炎症反应,从而放大和维持症状负担。这些结果强调,疾病的严重程度不能仅从病毒载量来推断,而是从免疫调节和 宿主 生理学之间的动态相互作用中得出。该框架为了解特定年龄的发病率提供了定量基础,并为设计针对免疫介导的病理学而不是单独的病毒复制的干预措施奠定了基础。

title: Mechanisms of ‘metabolizeaccretion’ and therapeutic targets in influenza infection
abstract: Influenza virus infection remains a leading cause of acute respiratory illness worldwide, with increasing resistance to conventional antiviral therapies highlighting the need for novel therapeutic strategies. This review introduces the concept of metabolizeaccretion, a self-reinforcing pathological cascade driven by metabolic reprogramming and characterized by three progressive stages: trigger, amplification, and persistence. During influenza infection, viral-induced alterations in glucose, lipid, amino acid, and purine metabolism lead to the aberrant accumulation of metabolic intermediates, which are associated with disrupted cellular energy homeostasis, altered inflammatory and immune responses, and potential epigenetic modifications that may stabilize pathological phenotypes. These processes collectively effect viral replication, immune evasion, and progression to severe respiratory damage. We further discuss potential therapeutic interventions targeting key metabolic enzymes, accumulated metabolites, gene expression regulation, and specific receptors to disrupt metabolizeaccretion. Finally, we emphasize the importance of multi-target approaches and precision medicine strategies to address metabolic heterogeneity in lung microenvironments, offering new insights for the treatment and management of influenza and related respiratory diseases.

These processes collectively effect viral replication, immune evasion, and progression to severe respiratory damage. We further discuss potential therapeutic interventions targeting key metabolic enzymes, accumulated metabolites, gene expression regulation, and specific receptors to disrupt metabolizeaccretion. Finally, we emphasize the importance of multi-target approaches and precision medicine strategies to address metabolic heterogeneity in lung microenvironments, offering new insights for the treatment and management of influenza and related respiratory diseases.

PEARLS Equine influenza virus at 70: What horses taught us about flu Laura Mojsiejczuk1, Thomas M. Chambers2, Pablo R. Murcia 1* 1 MRC-University of Glasgow Centre for Virus Research, Institute of Infection, Immunity and Inflammation, College of Medical, Veterinary and Life Sciences, University of Glasgow, Glasgow, Scotland, United Kingdom, 2 Department of Veterinary Science, Maxwell H. Gluck Equine Research Center, University of Kentucky, Lexington, Kentucky, United States of America * Pablo.Murcia@glasgow.ac.uk This year marks the 70th anniversary of the first documented isolation of equine influenza virus (EIV). In May 1956, major outbreaks of respiratory disease in horses took place in the former Republic of Czechoslovakia. The presence of antibodies against influenza A in serum from affected horses, together with observed similarities in clinical course with influenza in humans, led Sovinova and colleagues to “inves­ tigate the problem in greater detail”. Most nasal washes cultured in embryonated chicken eggs failed due to contamination, but sample 262 remained sterile, yielding A/equine/Prague/56 (H7N7) [1], marking the start of EIV research and initiating a new area of influenza research. While poultry and swine are also kept in dispersed, inter­ connected populations, horses uniquely combine those characteristics with a long lifespan and global mobility (trailing only humans as the most common commercial air travellers, for breeding and performance purposes), an intersection of epidemio­ logical features that more closely resembles that of humans and makes EIV a partic­ ularly informative model system. This Pearl article is our personal view that aims to highlight how studies on EIV have informed fundamental concepts of influenza virus biology, evolution, and epidemiology (Fig 1). Horses played a role in the history of human influenza Influenza A viruses (IAVs) exhibit a complex ecology rooted in their natural avian reservoir, from which multiple cross-species transmission events have led to docu­ mented spillover and host shifts from birds to mammals and also among mammalian species. Major human pandemics have arisen from such processes. Within this context, horses have historically been considered as potential sources of zoonotic infections. Influenza has been recognised as a disease of the horse since 1299 AD. Before the invention and widespread use of the automobile, contact rates between people and horses were much higher because horses were the main means of trans­ port. While empirical evidence is lacking, it has been suggested that horses played a role in the genesis of epidemic influenza [2] because human influenza epidemics were usually preceded by equine influenza outbreaks (importantly, this pattern dis­ appeared as horses were replaced by cars). Indeed, a recently published hypothesis PLOS Pathogens | https://doi.org/10.1371/journal.ppat.1014551 August 28, 2026 2 / 6 posed that horses may have contributed to the genesis of the virus that caused the 1918 pandemic [3], challenging conventional accounts. A second EIV subtype -this time an H3N8 virus- emerged in 1963 [4]. In 1965, Minuse and colleagues reported serological evidence of cross-reactive anti-H3 antibodies in individuals born between 1874 and 1891, predating the emergence of H3 IAVs in humans and pigs [5]. These findings supported the idea, already under discussion at the time, that influenza virus subtypes may “recycle” and that animal reservoirs could play a role in this process. EIV revealed the hidden diversity within individual hosts H3N8 EIV was used as a model system in pioneering studies aiming to elucidate the patterns of influenza within-host diversity and evolution. For decades, RNA viruses had been recognised as mixtures of genetic variants whose frequencies change rap­ idly during infection [6]. At a time when next-generation sequencing was in its infancy, clonal sequencing was combined with in vivo experiments in horses to measure for the first time the intra-host diversity of a mammalian IAV in its natural host. By iden­ tifying and counting mutations in the haemagglutinin gene of infected horses, those studies showed that acute equine influenza infections generate genetically distinct viral subpopulations beyond the consensus sequence and that most naturally arising mutations are deleterious [7]. It was also observed that some minority variants can persist for multiple days and even be transmitted, suggesting that virus transmission bottlenecks were not as narrow as previously perceived. These findings were later confirmed in natural outbreaks [8], also using clonal sequencing. EIV intra-host data contributed empirical evidence for the development of a within-host evolutionary model that, applied to H5N1 in the ferret transmission model, showed that respiratory droplet-transmissible variants can arise during a single mammalian infection, yet remain below consensus detection thresholds, and that the proportion reached by these variants determines the likelihood of onward transmis­ sion [9]. Since those early EIV studies based on the analyses of only a few thousand haemagglutinin sequences, advances in sequencing technologies (currently reaching millions of sequencing reads covering the entire genome) and bioinformatic pipelines have refined this picture, confirming that most within-host variants are short-lived, with strong purifying selection and genetic drift dominating evolutionary dynamics during acute infection. Furthermore, empirical estimates in large human cohorts suggest relatively tight transmission bottlenecks and limited evidence for sustained positive selection of antigenic variants during acute infection [10]. Comparative anal­ yses across viral models (e.g., dengue virus and cytomegalovirus) suggest that such constraints are not unique to influenza [6]. PLOS Pathogens | https://doi.org/10.1371/journal.ppat.1014551 August 28, 2026 3 / 6 phylogenies [11]. This theoretical framework has massively increased our understanding of infectious disease dynamics. As noted by Bryan Grenfell during the Commemorative lecture of the 2022 Kyoto Prize in Basic Science, the study of epidemics of influenza in horses stimulated ideas that became central to the theories in phylodynamics [12]. Data from experimental infections in horses were used to parameterise viral shedding and immune responses, enabling quantifica­ tion of the impact of viral fitness in the context of host immune status and determination of transmission probability [11]. EIV has also informed our understanding of long-term IAV evolution. Worobey et al. reconstructed the evolutionary history of IAV across multiple hosts and identified a synchronised global sweep of the internal genes of avian influenza viruses in the nineteenth century [13]. Notably, their analyses placed equine H7N7 as a basal sister lineage to avian, human, swine, and equine H3N8 clades. Interestingly, the branch that separates those sister lineages covers the 1866– 1878 period, which includes the major equine influenza epizootic of 1872 and leads Worobey and colleagues to speculate that “some epidemiological event” associated with that epizootic might have precipitated the global sweep of internal IAV genes. However, this proposal remains controversial: the back-extrapolation of any causal role for EIV or H7N7 in the broader emergence of mammalian and human influenza lacks direct empirical support. Timeline showing EIV-specific research milestones (upper track) and corresponding contributions to broader influenza and virology concepts (lower track) from 1956 to the present, which have shaped modern understanding of influenza across multiple host species. Icons adapted from Pixabay, PhyloPic.org, and Wikimedia Commons. Abbreviations: EIV, equine influenza virus; IAV, influenza A virus; R, effective reproduction number. https://doi.org/10.1371/journal.ppat.1014551.g001 PLOS Pathogens | https://doi.org/10.1371/journal.ppat.1014551 August 28, 2026 4 / 6 EIV documented decades of viral evolution in real time EIV offers a remarkably complete, real-time record of influenza virus macroevolution in a nonhuman mammal, from a putative avian spillover in 1963 that led to the emergence of H3N8 EIV (and subsequent replacement of the H7N7 sub­ type), through decades of enzootic diversification and competitive lineage turnover, and including a second host jump into dogs [14]. Canine influenza virus (CIV) was first reported in racing greyhounds in 2004. Unusually among mammalian influenza viruses, it emerged through the direct mammal-to-mammal transfer of an entire nonreassortant equine virus that then adapted to and circulated enzootically in dogs; it remains the first documented interspecies transfer with the donor species unequivocally identified by whole-genome sequencing. Sustained mainly by dense, interconnected shelter and kennel dog populations, H3N8 CIV never spread beyond North America, was last detected in 2016, and is presumed to be extinct [15]. Phylogenetic analyses of global H3N8 EIV complete genomes showed that distinct clades can co-circulate for extended periods, and that intra-subtype reassortment is relatively frequent, in addition to typical diversification driven by gradual substitutions on a single lineage observed in human IAVs. Notably, H3N8 EIV evolved at a slower rate than other mamma­ lian IAVs, potentially due to a weaker immune selection in its host population [16]. EIV taught us practical lessons about influenza control and eradication EIV research has also contributed to our general understanding of influenza epidemiology. Vaccine studies by the late Jennifer Mumford at the Animal Health Trust in Newmarket, United Kingdom, provided important information regard­ ing vaccine composition (in terms of viral strains to be included as well as adjuvants) and duration of vaccine-mediated immunity, which in turn informed vaccination schedules. While this research contributed significantly to the development of measures to control equine influenza, data generated by those highly controlled experimental infections informed epidemi­ ological models that explicitly measured, for the first time, how amino acid differences between immunising and circulating influenza strains impact on the effective reproductive number R, and as a result on epidemic size [17]. Beyond controlled experiments, population-level genomic analyses revealed that EIV displayed a significant drop in global genetic diversity after vaccination became mandatory in competition horses in the early 1980s, providing a field- scale example of interventions causing measurable population bottlenecks [16]. In Australia, a large EIV outbreak in 2007 affected more than 70,000 horses, but the virus was later eradicated by a combination of zoning, movement restrictions, vaccination (using DIVA vaccines, see below) and increased biosecurity [18]. To the best of our knowledge, this remains the only documented case of active eradication of a mammalian IAV following widespread introduction into a country. A recent study suggests that EIV could be eradicated from the United Kingdom, as continuous endemic transmission might not be supported [19]. As with human IAVs, vaccination is the best prophylactic measure recommended- and sometimes required- for horses at risk of exposure, such as by travel to competitions. Several EIV vaccine platforms are available, including inactivated virus, ISCOM-based, modified-live virus, and recombinant canarypox-vectored vaccines, and plant-based virus-like particles expressing HA, which offer a potentially viable alternative, as they are easier to update and produce [20]. The recombinant canarypox-vectored vaccines enable differentiation of infected from vaccinated animals (DIVA), a capability that was essential during the 2007 epizootic eradication campaign in Australia. EIV undergoes antigenic drift, though at a slower rate than human IAVs. Furthermore, vaccine strains are updated less frequently than those for human seasonal influenza, likely due to limited virological and economic incentives associated with the relatively small veterinary market. Conclusion In sum, the study of EIV has made a significant contribution to our current understanding of influenza virus infections not only in horses but also in other mammalian hosts (including humans), illustrating the importance of comparative approaches in virology research. analysis.research_question_and_background: This study explores how research on equine influenza virus (EIV) has contributed to understanding fundamental aspects of influenza virus biology, evolution, and epidemiology, particularly in relation to human seasonal influenza viruses.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study is a narrative review of historical and contemporary research on equine influenza virus, focusing on its role as a model system for understanding influenza dynamics. It includes data from outbreaks in horses and comparisons with human influenza.
analysis.methods: The authors conducted a comprehensive review of literature and historical records related to equine influenza virus, analyzing its epidemiological features, genetic evolution, and interactions with host populations. They compared EIV with human influenza viruses to identify parallels and differences in transmission and pathogenesis.
analysis.main_results: The study highlights that equine influenza virus has provided critical insights into influenza virus ecology, evolution, and host interactions, particularly due to its unique epidemiological characteristics resembling those of human seasonal influenza viruses.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpret that EIV has been a valuable model for studying influenza, offering a unique perspective on viral transmission and evolution. This is a novel contribution to understanding how animal models can inform human influenza research.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings suggest that studying equine influenza virus can enhance our understanding of human seasonal influenza, aiding in the development of more effective surveillance, diagnosis, and control strategies for human influenza.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is based on historical and observational data, which may introduce limitations in the strength of evidence. However, the authors provide a well-supported narrative grounded in multiple documented studies and comparisons with human influenza.

analysis.summary_en: This study examines the historical and scientific contributions of equine influenza virus (EIV) to understanding influenza virus biology, evolution, and epidemiology. It highlights how EIV, with its unique characteristics such as global mobility and long lifespan, serves as an informative model for human seasonal influenza. The authors review key findings from EIV research, emphasizing its role in elucidating cross-species transmission and host interactions. They argue that insights from EIV studies have informed fundamental concepts in influenza research, offering a novel perspective on the virus's behavior. The study underscores the importance of animal models in understanding human influenza, with implications for surveillance and control strategies. However, the reliance on historical data and observational studies limits the strength of the evidence, though the analysis remains grounded in well-documented findings.

elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 该研究是一项关于马流感病毒的历史与当代研究的叙述性综述,重点关注其作为理解流感动态的模型系统的作用。研究纳入了来自暴发马匹的数据,并与人流感进行了比较。
elements_zh.methods: 作者对与马流感病毒相关的文献和历史记录进行了全面综述,分析了其流行病学特征、遗传进化及其与宿主宿主种群的相互作用。他们将马流感病毒与人流感病毒进行了比较,以识别在传播和发病机制方面的相似之处与差异。
elements_zh.main_results: 该研究强调,马流感病毒为流感病毒生态学、进化 和 宿主 相互作用提供了重要见解,特别是由于其独特的流行病学特征类似于人类 季节性流感 病毒。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 作者解释说,EIV 是研究流感的一个有价值的模型,为病毒 传播 和 进化 提供了独特的视角。这是了解动物模型如何为人类流感研究提供信息的新颖贡献。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 研究结果表明,研究马流感病毒可以增强我们对人类 季节性流感 的了解,有助于开发更有效的 监测、诊断 和人类流感控制策略。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该研究基于历史和观察性数据,可能在证据强度方面存在局限性。然而,作者基于多项已记录研究及与人流感的比较,提供了一份支持充分的叙述性综述。

title: Newton Divided Difference Optimization for Fingerprint-Based Neural Virtual Screening against Avian Influenza A/H9N2
abstract: Avian influenza A/H9N2 poses persistent zoonotic and veterinary threats, yet efficient computational tools for antiviral compound prioritization remain underdeveloped, particularly with respect to optimizer behavior in high-dimensional neural screening. This study proposes Newton Divided Difference (NDD) optimization, a lightweight positive diagonal curvature-aware training strategy, as a novel optimizer for fingerprint-based neural virtual screening against avian influenza A/H9N2, with the objective of evaluating its performance across aligned molecular fingerprint representations and chemically structured validation protocols. An aligned benchmark of 1,459 molecules consisting of 615 candidate active compounds and 844 decoys was represented by EState (79 features), PubChem (881 features), and Klekota–Roth (4,860 features) fingerprints, sharing identical molecule identities, labels, and split assignments. A fixed multilayer perceptron (MLP) classifier was trained with NDD and seven baseline optimizers under stratified, scaffold-key, and similarity-cluster split protocols across five repeated seeds. NDD achieved the highest descriptive ROC-AUC (Receiver Operating Characteriztic – Area Under the Curve) and PR-AUC (Precision-Recall Area Under the Curve) on Klekota–Roth fingerprints under scaffold-key and similarity-cluster protocols, and remained competitive under the stratified split with ROC-AUC of 0.9872. Architecture-sensitivity tests confirmed stable NDD performance across multiple network configurations, with ROC-AUC values ranging from 0.9876 to 0.9890. Compared with Hessian-free optimization, NDD reduced per-run runtime from approximately 50–54 seconds to approximately 8 seconds on Klekota–Roth under the same CPU-only configuration while achieving comparable ranking performance. The novelty of this work lies in the first systematic assessment of NDD for H9N2 neural virtual screening, demonstrating that positive diagonal curvature-aware scaling provides a practical, stable, and computationally efficient optimization alternative in sparse high-dimensional ligand-based screening settings, although external validation and prospective experimental confirmation remain necessary before practical antiviral prioritization.

full_text: Abstract Background Influenza exhibits pronounced seasonal and geographical heterogeneity, suggesting that meteorological factors play a key regulatory role in influenza transmission. However, whether different influenza subtypes possess distinct meteorological drivers remains unclear, and systematic evidence from temperate continental monsoon climate regions is relatively scarce. Methods Based on laboratory-confirmed influenza surveillance data and concurrent meteorological data from Shanxi Province during 2009–2024 (excluding the period of COVID-19 non-pharmaceutical interventions), a multi-step analytical approach was employed to systematically evaluate the meteorological drivers of influenza A(H1N1)pdm09, A(H3N2), and B viruses. First, a two-stage random forest was used to identify key meteorological variables. Second, univariate analysis was performed to determine the optimal lag structures for each factor, and multivariate logistic regression models were constructed to identify independent effects. Finally, joint effect analysis was conducted to explore synergistic and antagonistic effects among meteorological factors. Results A total of 29,246 laboratory-confirmed influenza cases were identified during the study period, with A(H1N1)pdm09, A(H3N2), and B accounting for 28.7%, 39.6%, and 31.7%, respectively. Absolute humidity emerged as the most robust protective factor across all subtypes. The three subtypes exhibited distinct meteorological driver patterns: A(H1N1)pdm09 was sensitive to low temperature, low humidity, and high wind speed, with the risk effect of high wind speed being reversed by high temperature; A(H3N2) was primarily regulated by higher solar radiation and higher temperature, which exhibited a synergistic protective effect; B was closely associated with the humidity‒pressure system, with high humidity offsetting the risk effect of high pressure. Conclusions Influenza subtypes exhibit differential responses to meteorological factors, with complex synergistic and antagonistic effects among these factors. These findings suggest that the development of influenza meteorological early warning models should consider subtype specificity and multi-factor interactions, rather than relying on single universal indicators. Clinical trial number Not applicable. (As this study is not a clinical trial.) analysis.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to investigate the differential meteorological drivers of influenza subtypes in Shanxi Province, China, as influenza exhibits pronounced seasonal and geographical heterogeneity, suggesting that meteorological factors play a key regulatory role in influenza transmission.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study used laboratory-confirmed influenza surveillance data and concurrent meteorological data from Shanxi Province during 2009–2024, excluding the period of COVID-19 non-pharmaceutical interventions. It focused on influenza A(H1N1)pdm09, A(H3N2), and B viruses, with a total of 29,246 cases identified during the study period.
analysis.methods: A multi-step analytical approach was employed, including a two-stage random forest to identify key meteorological variables, univariate analysis to determine optimal lag structures, and multivariate logistic regression models to identify independent effects. Joint effect analysis was also conducted to explore synergistic and antagonistic effects among meteorological factors.
analysis.main_results: A total of 29,246 laboratory-confirmed influenza cases were identified, with A(H1N1)pdm09, A(H3N2), and B accounting for 28.7%, 39.6%, and 31.7%, respectively. Absolute humidity emerged as the most robust protective factor across all subtypes. The three subtypes exhibited distinct meteorological driver patterns, with A(H1N1)pdm09 sensitive to low temperature, low humidity, and high wind speed; A(H3N2) primarily regulated by higher solar radiation and temperature; and B closely associated with the humidity‒pressure system.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The findings suggest that influenza subtypes exhibit differential responses to meteorological factors, with complex synergistic and antagonistic effects among these factors, highlighting the need for subtype-specific models in meteorological early warning systems.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The results can inform the development of more accurate influenza meteorological early warning models, which could improve surveillance and public health preparedness by accounting for subtype-specific meteorological drivers.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study excluded the period of COVID-19 non-pharmaceutical interventions, which may have affected influenza transmission patterns. The evidence is moderate, as the findings are based on observational data and statistical analysis rather than experimental intervention.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigated the differential meteorological drivers of influenza subtypes in Shanxi Province, China, from 2009 to 2024. It found that influenza A(H1N1)pdm09, A(H3N2), and B viruses responded differently to meteorological factors, with A(H1N1)pdm09 being sensitive to low temperature, low humidity, and high wind speed; A(H3N2) primarily regulated by higher solar radiation and temperature; and B closely associated with the humidity‒pressure system. The results suggest that subtype-specific meteorological early warning models are necessary for improved surveillance and public health preparedness. The study used a multi-step analytical approach, including random forest, univariate analysis, and multivariate logistic regression models. However, the exclusion of the COVID-19 period and reliance on observational data limit the confidence in the findings, resulting in a moderate evidence assessment.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 该研究旨在调查中国山西省流感亚型的差异气象驱动因素,因为流感表现出明显的季节和地理异质性,表明气象因素在流感 传播 中发挥着关键的调节作用。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 该研究使用了2009-2024年山西省实验室确认的流感监测数据和同期气象数据,不包括COVID-19非药物干预期间。该研究重点关注流感 甲型H1N1流感病毒pdm09、甲型H3N2流感病毒 和 B 病毒,研究期间共发现 29,246 例病例。
elements_zh.methods: 采用多步骤分析方法,包括两阶段随机森林来识别关键气象变量,单变量分析来确定最佳滞后结构,以及多元逻辑回归模型来识别独立效应。还进行了联合效应分析,探讨气象因素之间的协同作用和拮抗作用。
elements_zh.main_results: 共确诊流感实验室确诊病例29246例,其中甲型H1N1流感病毒pdm09、甲型H3N2流感病毒、B型分别占28.7%、39.6%、31.7%。绝对湿度成为所有亚型中最强大的保护因素。3个亚型表现出不同的气象驱动模式,甲型H1N1流感病毒pdm09对低温、低湿、大风速敏感;甲型H3N2流感病毒 主要受较高的太阳辐射和温度调节;B与湿度-压力系统密切相关。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 研究结果表明,流感亚型对气象因素表现出不同的反应,这些因素之间存在复杂的协同和拮抗作用,凸显了气象预警系统中亚型特异性模型的必要性。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 研究结果可以为开发更准确的流感气象预警模型提供信息,该模型可以通过考虑特定亚型的气象驱动因素来改善 监测 和公共卫生准备工作。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该研究排除了 COVID-19 非药物干预期间,这可能影响了流感 传播 模式。证据是中等的,因为研究结果是基于观察数据和统计分析而不是实验干预。

It focused on influenza A(H1N1)pdm09, A(H3N2), and B viruses, with a total of 29,246 cases identified during the study period.
analysis_en.methods: A multi-step analytical approach was employed, including a two-stage random forest to identify key meteorological variables, univariate analysis to determine optimal lag structures, and multivariate logistic regression models to identify independent effects. Joint effect analysis was also conducted to explore synergistic and antagonistic effects among meteorological factors.
analysis_en.main_results: A total of 29,246 laboratory-confirmed influenza cases were identified, with A(H1N1)pdm09, A(H3N2), and B accounting for 28.7%, 39.6%, and 31.7%, respectively. Absolute humidity emerged as the most robust protective factor across all subtypes. The three subtypes exhibited distinct meteorological driver patterns, with A(H1N1)pdm09 sensitive to low temperature, low humidity, and high wind speed; A(H3N2) primarily regulated by higher solar radiation and temperature; and B closely associated with the humidity‒pressure system.
analysis_en.interpretation_and_novelty: The findings suggest that influenza subtypes exhibit differential responses to meteorological factors, with complex synergistic and antagonistic effects among these factors, highlighting the need for subtype-specific models in meteorological early warning systems.
analysis_en.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The results can inform the development of more accurate influenza meteorological early warning models, which could improve surveillance and public health preparedness by accounting for subtype-specific meteorological drivers.
analysis_en.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study excluded the period of COVID-19 non-pharmaceutical interventions, which may have affected influenza transmission patterns. The evidence is moderate, as the findings are based on observational data and statistical analysis rather than experimental intervention.

analysis_zh.study_design_and_population: 该研究使用了2009-2024年山西省实验室确认的流感监测数据和同期气象数据,不包括COVID-19非药物干预期间。该研究重点关注流感 甲型H1N1流感病毒pdm09、甲型H3N2流感病毒 和 B 病毒,研究期间共发现 29,246 例病例。
analysis_zh.methods: 采用多步骤分析方法,包括两阶段随机森林来识别关键气象变量,单变量分析来确定最佳滞后结构,以及多元逻辑回归模型来识别独立效应。还进行了联合效应分析,探讨气象因素之间的协同作用和拮抗作用。
analysis_zh.main_results: 共确诊流感实验室确诊病例29246例,其中甲型H1N1流感病毒pdm09、甲型H3N2流感病毒、B型分别占28.7%、39.6%、31.7%。绝对湿度成为所有亚型中最强大的保护因素。3个亚型表现出不同的气象驱动模式,甲型H1N1流感病毒pdm09对低温、低湿、大风速敏感;甲型H3N2流感病毒 主要受较高的太阳辐射和温度调节;B与湿度-压力系统密切相关。

full_text: Abstract Respiratory tract infections (RTIs) remain a major cause of morbidity worldwide owing to their diverse etiologies and overlapping clinical presentations. Multiplex real-time polymerase chain reaction (RT-qPCR) enables simultaneous detection of multiple respiratory pathogens and provides comprehensive epidemiological data. Following the COVID-19 pandemic, alterations in respiratory pathogen circulation and increasing recognition of viral–bacterial co-detection have highlighted the need for updated molecular epidemiological surveillance. This retrospective cross-sectional study included consecutive nasopharyngeal swab specimens obtained from patients with clinically suspected RTIs who underwent multiplex RT-qPCR testing at Siirt Training and Research Hospital, Türkiye, between January 2024 and December 2025. Patients were stratified into predefined age groups. Positive specimens were classified into mutually exclusive viral-only, bacterial-only, and viral–bacterial co-detection categories. Multivariable logistic regression analysis was performed to identify independent factors associated with respiratory pathogen detection. Among 1,666 nasopharyngeal swab specimens, respiratory pathogens were detected in 1,166 (70.0%). Bacterial-only detection accounted for 473 (40.6%), viral-only detection for 395 (33.9%), and viral–bacterial co-detection for 298 (25.6%) of positive specimens. Streptococcus pneumoniae and Haemophilus influenzae were the most frequently detected bacterial pathogens, whereas human rhinovirus and influenza A virus predominated among viral pathogens. Children had significantly higher odds of respiratory pathogen detection than adults (aOR 2.27, 95% CI 1.72–2.99; p < 0.001). Respiratory pathogen detection also varied significantly by season, with significantly lower odds during summer (aOR 0.58, 95% CI 0.43–0.78; p < 0.001) and autumn (aOR 0.57, 95% CI 0.43–0.75; p < 0.001) than during winter. Respiratory pathogen detection during the post-pandemic period demonstrated distinct age-related and seasonal patterns together with frequent viral–bacterial co-detection. Separate evaluation of viral-only, bacterial-only, and viral–bacterial co-detection provided a more comprehensive understanding of respiratory pathogen epidemiology. Because multiplex RT-qPCR detects microbial nucleic acids rather than confirming active infection, bacterial detections—particularly for common nasopharyngeal colonizers—should be interpreted together with clinical findings and complementary microbiological investigations. analysis.summary_en: This study investigated the age and seasonal patterns of respiratory pathogens, particularly influenza viruses, and their co-detections in a post-pandemic setting using multiplex RT-qPCR. Conducted at Siirt Training and Research Hospital in Türkiye between January 2024 and December 2025, the study included 1,666 nasopharyngeal swab specimens. Respiratory pathogens were detected in 70.0% of specimens, with bacterial-only, viral-only, and co-detection categories accounting for 40.6%, 33.9%, and 25.6% respectively. Children had significantly higher odds of pathogen detection than adults, and detection rates were lower during summer and autumn compared to winter. The study highlights the importance of evaluating viral-only, bacterial-only, and co-detection patterns for a comprehensive understanding of respiratory pathogen epidemiology. However, the retrospective design and lack of prospective data limit the depth of clinical interpretation, resulting in moderate evidence strength.

source_body_en: This retrospective cross-sectional study included consecutive nasopharyngeal swab specimens obtained from patients with clinically suspected RTIs who underwent multiplex RT-qPCR testing at Siirt Training and Research Hospital, Türkiye, between January 2024 and December 2025. Because multiplex RT-qPCR detects microbial nucleic acids rather than confirming active infection, bacterial detections—particularly for common nasopharyngeal colonizers—should be interpreted together with clinical findings and complementary microbiological investigations. Ethics approval and consent to participate This study was approved by the Siirt University Non-Interventional Clinical Research Ethics Committee (Decision No: 2026/01/03/4 Decision Date: 02.03.2026). Due to the retrospective design of the study and the use of anonymized data, the requirement for informed consent to participate was waived by the Siirt University Non-Interventional Clinical Research Ethics Committee. This applies to all patients and all patient data included in the study. The study was conducted in accordance with the Declaration of Helsinki. analysis_zh.research_question_and_background: 该研究旨在调查呼吸道病原体(特别是流感病毒)的年龄和季节模式,以及它们在大流行后环境中的共同检测,因为呼吸道感染由于其病因多样且临床表现重叠,仍然是一个重要的公共卫生问题。
analysis_zh.study_design_and_population: 这项回顾性横断面研究分析了 2024 年 1 月至 2025 年 12 月土耳其 Siirt 培训和研究医院临床疑似 RTI 患者的连续鼻咽拭子标本。患者被分为预定义的年龄组。
analysis_zh.methods: 该研究使用多重 RT-qPCR 检测呼吸道病原体,并进行多变量逻辑回归分析,以确定与病原体检测相关的独立因素,包括年龄和季节。
analysis_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 研究结果表明,呼吸道病原体检测存在明显的年龄相关和季节性模式,包括频繁的病毒-细菌联合检测,这提供了对这些病原体的 流行病学 的更全面的了解。
analysis_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 结果可以为改进的 监测 策略提供信息,增强诊断方法,并指导有针对性的公共卫生干预措施,以解决呼吸道感染的季节性变化和特定年龄风险。
analysis_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该研究的回顾性设计和对匿名数据的依赖可能会限制临床解释的深度,并且由于缺乏前瞻性数据和潜在的混杂因素,证据是中等的。
